sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: Framework only: recognizing containers is not implementing a security protocol. Exactly two parts and required protocol dispatch. Unknown protocol cannot be processed as protected content.

sections.title: Definition of Security Subtypes of Multipart
sections.audit: Signed places control second; encrypted places control first. Descriptive processing stages defer exact algorithms to protocol profile.

sections.title: Definition of Multipart/Signed
sections.audit: Signed requires boundary/protocol/micalg and exactly two parts. Signature covers first part including its MIME headers, not enclosing headers or external references. Control type matches protocol. Conflicting micalg and control algorithm is an error. Signed container stays opaque in transit; transfer re-encoding invalidates protection. SMTP-compatible signed generation uses7bit-safe encodings. Verify profile-defined bytes before displaying authenticated content.

sections.title: Definition of Multipart/Encrypted
sections.audit: Encrypted requires boundary/protocol and exactly two parts: control first and application/octet-stream ciphertext second. Inner MIME headers encrypted with content. Do not render ciphertext or failed decryption output as a MIME message. Encryption alone does not establish sender authentication or integrity; selected protocol must define those.

sections.title: Definition of Control Information Content Types
sections.audit: Protocol specification must precisely define control media type, contents and processing. MIME registration alone is not a crypto suite.

sections.title: Definition of Key Management Content Types
sections.audit: Key request/response body parts are an optional distribution design, not a defined exchange, authentication scheme or invisible delivery guarantee.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.audit: Size declaration enables early rejection, not guaranteed acceptance.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: Large MIME objects motivate resource negotiation; this does not define application content limits.

sections.title: Framework for the Size Declaration Extension
sections.audit: SIZE advertisement may omit its decimal limit. Zero means no fixed maximum; omission means unknown maximum. MAIL SIZE has1–20 digits and occurs once; command-line allowance grows26 characters.

sections.title: The Message Size Declaration service extension
sections.audit: Advertised fixed limits permit early permanent rejection. Temporary storage limits remain possible.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.audit: Count message octets including headers and CRLF, excluding DATA terminator and extra dot-stuffing octets. Count encoded transmitted representation, not decoded attachment size.

sections.title: The extended MAIL command
sections.audit: Declared size is ideally exact, otherwise a generally conservative estimate. It MUST NOT delimit DATA.

sections.title: Server action on receipt of the extended MAIL command
sections.audit: 452 means temporary storage shortage;552 means fixed-size excess. Server may accept an underestimated message but need not.

sections.title: Client action on receiving response to extended MAIL command
sections.audit: Reset or quit after rejection; retry temporary failure later, report permanent failure. MAIL250 does not guarantee DATA or final acceptance.

sections.title: Messages larger than the declared size.
sections.audit: An underestimated message may fail after transfer. An accepted declaration should not later receive size-based552 unless actual size exceeds declaration.

sections.title: Per-recipient rejection based on message size.
sections.audit: Size failures can be per recipient. Requeue452 recipients, not permanent552 recipients, while preserving successful recipients.

sections.title: Minimal usage
sections.audit: Minimal client may compare advertised size only. Minimal server still accepts extended MAIL. An omitted advertised limit requires resource checking before positive response to declared size.

sections.title: Example
sections.audit: Example exercises mixed recipient outcomes and later DATA acceptance; no all-recipient success inference.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: Resource declarations can facilitate denial of service; enforce actual consumption limits independently of claims.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: POP downloads a maildrop; it is not a server conversation database or multi-folder synchronization protocol.

sections.title: A Short Digression
sections.audit: Submission is separate from retrieval and may use a different relay; historical relay advice does not define current submission authentication.

sections.title: Basic Operation
sections.audit: State transitions, CRLF framing, dot stuffing, uppercase status and 512-octet single-line responses reviewed. Inactivity timeout is at least ten minutes and does not enter UPDATE. Generic negative replies do not distinguish unsupported commands from temporary inability.

sections.title: The AUTHORIZATION State
sections.audit: Authentication precedes maildrop locking and transaction state. Message numbers are assigned within the opened maildrop; they are not persistent event identities. QUIT here does not delete mail.

sections.title: The TRANSACTION State
sections.audit: STAT/LIST exclude marked messages; RETR returns complete dot-stuffed content; DELE only marks; NOOP changes nothing; RSET clears deletion marks. All command arguments, responses and examples reviewed.

sections.title: The UPDATE State
sections.audit: Only transaction QUIT enters UPDATE. Deletion errors may remove some or none of marked messages; abnormal termination must not perform UPDATE deletion. Retry must tolerate uncertain outcomes.

sections.title: Optional POP3 Commands
sections.audit: TOP, UIDL, USER, PASS and APOP fully reviewed. UIDL persists across sessions, allows identical copies to share an ID, and verified erratum529 extends nonreuse to the maildrop lifetime. Preview and authentication identifiers are not message authorship evidence.

sections.title: Scaling and Operational Considerations
sections.audit: Quota and site retention can remove read or unread messages outside ordinary protocol deletion; download-once policy requires durable storage before successful session completion. POP lacks general folder/push semantics.

sections.title: POP3 Command Summary
sections.audit: Command summary reviewed; its placement of USER/PASS under minimal commands conflicts with Section7 and AppendixA making them optional. Do not infer a required plaintext authentication method from this table.

sections.title: Example POP3 Session
sections.audit: Complete example session reviewed; its clear transport and APOP flow are historical examples, not Email Next security recommendations.

sections.title: Message Format
sections.audit: Size reflects CRLF message representation and excludes extra dot-stuffing octets. Local storage line endings are not the transmitted byte representation.

sections.title: References
sections.audit: All references reviewed; historical SMTP, message format, MD5, IMAP and AUTH dependencies require separate applicability/current-successor work.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: Clear passwords/mail, username enumeration and historical APOP security assumptions reviewed. None establishes endpoint identity or protects modern Email Next transport by itself.

sections.title: Acknowledgements
sections.audit: Acknowledgments and historical lineage reviewed; no additional protocol behavior.

sections.title: Authors' Addresses
sections.audit: Author end matter reviewed; no protocol requirements.

sections.title: Observations

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: CAPA advertises optional server behavior; it does not discover recipient encryption or rendering support.

sections.title: General Command and Response Grammar
sections.audit: Command/response grammar reviewed; printed ASCII ranges include DEL despite printable comments, and greeting grammar omits conventional spaces. These discrepancies are not adopted as new Email Next syntax.

sections.title: Parameter and Response Lengths
sections.audit: CAPA-supporting servers accept commands up to 255 octets including CRLF, or larger supported-extension limits; first response line remains 512 octets.

sections.title: The CAPA Command
sections.audit: CAPA works before and after authentication; tags are case-insensitive, values can change by state, and integrity-protected authentication calls for rechecking capabilities against active downgrades.

sections.title: Initial Set of Capabilities
sections.audit: Initial capabilities reviewed; APOP uses the greeting challenge rather than a duplicate CAPA tag.

sections.title: TOP capability
sections.audit: TOP means optional header/body-prefix retrieval support, not complete-message validation.

sections.title: USER capability
sections.audit: USER advertises USER/PASS support without promising availability for every account.

sections.title: SASL capability
sections.audit: SASL advertises AUTH mechanisms and initial-response support; historical mechanisms are not a present security recommendation.

sections.title: RESP-CODES capability
sections.audit: RESP-CODES marks bracket-prefixed response text as machine-readable protocol status.

sections.title: LOGIN-DELAY capability
sections.audit: LOGIN-DELAY gives seconds since successful authentication; preauthentication value is the largest possible account value, with USER indicating a useful authenticated refresh.

sections.title: PIPELINING capability
sections.audit: Pipelined commands execute and match responses in order; blocking writes must respect transport windows. This does not order conversation events across devices.

sections.title: EXPIRE capability
sections.audit: EXPIRE gives minimum retention, with deliberately imprecise starting time; zero permits implicit deletion of RETR messages on UPDATE. Preauthentication value is the smallest possible retention.

sections.title: UIDL capability
sections.audit: UIDL advertises optional retrieval identifiers; it does not supply endpoint-authenticated event IDs.

sections.title: IMPLEMENTATION capability
sections.audit: IMPLEMENTATION is diagnostic identification; clients must not select behavior from this string.

sections.title: Future Extensions to POP3
sections.audit: POP remains download-and-delete; mailbox/upload extensions are discouraged. Basic retrieval cannot depend on arbitrary additional capabilities.

sections.title: Extended POP3 Response Codes
sections.audit: Hierarchical case-insensitive response codes permit unknown detail to be ignored; human-readable text is not a recipient-capability channel.

sections.title: Initial POP3 response codes
sections.audit: Initial failure classifications reviewed separately from cryptographic policy.

sections.title: The LOGIN-DELAY response code
sections.audit: LOGIN-DELAY on USER can disclose account existence and should be avoided under the described conditions.

sections.title: The IN-USE response code
sections.audit: IN-USE means authentication succeeded but the maildrop is busy; it is not evidence of lost encryption support.

sections.audit: Capability and response-code registration requirements reviewed; no Email Next POP capability is registered by this draft.

sections.title: Overview
sections.audit: CHUNKING avoids DATA sentinel scanning; BINARYMIME separately avoids transport-encoding overhead. Neither changes application semantics or authentication.

sections.title: Framework for the Large Message Extensions
sections.audit: CHUNKING advertises BDAT, which counts exact canonical message octets and sends data immediately. Collect MAIL/RCPT outcomes first. Each chunk has a reply; zero-length LAST allowed. Failure requires consuming/discarding the declared chunk and already-pipelined chunks, stopping new chunks and RSET. Do not mix DATA/BDAT in one transaction. DATA support remains required. Incorrect lengths desynchronize parsing.

sections.title: Framework for the Binary Service Extension
sections.audit: BINARYMIME requires CHUNKING and BODY=BINARYMIME; preserve every content octet. DATA is forbidden for this body mode. MIME text canonicalization still applies. Unsupported downstream binary requires lossless valid conversion or permanent failure; no nested transfer encodings. The source explicitly says accept improperly declared Binary CTE then recommends a DSN; this is not permission to send unnegotiated binary. Protected-byte changes remain constrained by the selected security profile.

sections.title: Content-Transfer-Encoding restrictions

Preserve meaningful spaces through encoding; whitespace-only headers must not become accidental header/body separators. From-space protection recommended. Encryption-only allowance is distinct. Accepting received encodings does not authorize canonical-byte guessing.

sections.title: OpenPGP signed data

Detachedsignature coversheadersandencodedbody. Boundary-precedingCRLF belongsdelimiter,notautomaticallysigneddata; absentfinalCRLFmustnotbeinvented. sections.audit: STARTTLS advertises an argument-free EHLO capability and adds an argument-free command.

sections.title: The STARTTLS Keyword
sections.audit: Advertisement means current ability to negotiate, not endpoint identity or downstream protection.

sections.title: The STARTTLS Command
sections.audit: 220 begins TLS before further SMTP;501 rejects parameters;454 follows local transport policy. STARTTLS ends a pipeline group. Base public-MX interoperability rule differs from submission/relay authentication policy; later transport-policy standards require separate audit.

sections.title: Processing After the STARTTLS Command
sections.audit: Evaluate achieved authentication and privacy before continuing. Insufficient protection leads to termination/refusal, not a protection badge. Historical certificate guidance is updated by7817 and later identity standards.

sections.title: Result of the STARTTLS Command
sections.audit: Reset SMTP state after handshake; discard pre-TLS peer/session knowledge and issue fresh EHLO. Capabilities may change. Do not advertise or invoke STARTTLS inside an active TLS session.

sections.title: STARTTLS on the Submission Port
sections.audit: Submission can use STARTTLS; current submission/TLS recommendations require separate audit.

sections.title: Usage Example
sections.audit: Example correctly issues a new EHLO after TLS and removes STARTTLS from the new advertisement.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: Hop TLS is not end-to-end confidentiality or message authorship. Stripping/altering STARTTLS is an active attack; required-TLS configuration must resist fallback. Enforce actual negotiated policy and discard insecure session observations.

sections.title: Introduction

sections.title: The Format and DelSp Parameters
sections.audit: Format and DelSp case-insensitive. Missing/unknown Format means fixed; missing/unknown DelSp means no. Ignore DelSp outside flowed plain text. Transfer decoding precedes interpretation.

sections.title: Interpreting Format=Flowed
sections.audit: Count initial quote marks before removing one stuffing space; trailing SP marks flow except signature separator. DelSp=yes removes exactly one trailing SP. Preserve other spaces. End paragraph on depth change, signature boundary or body end, including malformed input.

sections.title: Generating Format=Flowed
sections.audit: Generation uses soft SP CRLF, correct DelSp for wrapping method, mandatory stuffing, equal quote depth per paragraph and no accidental signature separator. 78-character recommendation includes stuffing; long unbroken words exception does not waive SMTP hard limits. QP discouraged except necessity or cryptographic protection.

sections.title: Usenet Signature Convention
sections.audit: DASH DASH SP separator is neither fixed nor flowed. Recognize before quotation processing and after quoted stuffing removal; never absorb into paragraph. Separator is not authority to discard subsequent answers.

sections.title: Space-Stuffing
sections.audit: Remove one stuffing SP after quote detection; stuffed literal > is not quotation. Protect From-space and leading-space lines.

sections.title: Quoting
sections.audit: Initial consecutive > count sets depth; > > has depth1, not2. Depth wins over malformed flow across quote boundaries. Rewrap dequoted content and restore exact depth.

sections.title: Digital Signatures and Encryption

sections.title: Interoperability

sections.title: Trailing White Space Corruption

sections.title: When (not) to send automatic responses
sections.audit: Never answer every message. Suppress automatic traffic, null destinations and malformed requests; bound responses and avoid unauthenticated side effects. Seven-day advice concerns absence notices, not a universal protocol timer. Recipient-header heuristic is not reliable evidence of Bcc membership.

sections.title: Format of automatic responses
sections.audit: Header, body and envelope requirements apply independently.

sections.title: Message header
sections.audit: Response headers identify the responder and causal message without authenticating either.

sections.title: From field
sections.audit: Use a configured public identity; do not derive or disclose login names, internal hosts or private aliases. Provide an operator contact appropriate to responder type.

sections.title: Reply-To field
sections.audit: Reply-To can designate an expected service reply, but requires loop prevention; it is not generic authorization to send automatic replies.

sections.title: To field
sections.audit: Single response recipient limits amplification. Never negotiate by reply-all.

sections.title: Date field
sections.audit: Response Date is generation time, not subject delivery time or evidence of online presence.

sections.title: Subject field
sections.audit: Auto: is a human hint, not a protocol detector. Preserve encoded-word boundaries and header line limits.

sections.title: In-Reply-To and References fields
sections.audit: Generate causal reply headers from Message-ID under message-format rules; these do not establish authenticated event identity.

sections.title: Auto-Submitted field
sections.audit: Automatic direct responses carry Auto-Submitted: auto-replied.

sections.title: Precedence field
sections.audit: Precedence is nonstandard and cannot ensure suppression or invisibility.

sections.title: Message content
sections.audit: Keep personal/group replies short and readable; do not reflect attachments or substantial attacker content. Service payloads need their own bounded format.

sections.title: Use of DSNs and MDNs instead of this specification
sections.audit: DSNs describe delivery and MDNs disposition. Neither is a camouflage format for key exchange.

sections.title: Message envelope
sections.audit: Use a loop-safe envelope, including a null reverse-path where applicable; request NOTIFY=NEVER only when DSN is supported. Suppression does not confirm delivery.

sections.title: Where to send automatic responses (and where not to send them)
sections.audit: Generic post-delivery replies use Return-Path; pre-delivery replies use envelope reverse-path. Service-specific alternative destinations require precise specification. Do not fall back to From, Reply-To or Sender heuristics. Verified erratum223 removes accidental > before From.

sections.title: The Auto-Submitted header field
sections.audit: Auto-Submitted marks automatic origin and supports filtering; it grants no deletion, hidden-delivery or authentication semantics.

sections.title: Syntax
sections.audit: At most one field; parse optional parameters and CFWS under referenced grammars. Conflicting duplicates are unsuitable for automatic activation.

sections.title: Semantics
sections.audit: Distinguish auto-generated initiation from auto-replied response and human-originated no. Unknown non-no keywords still indicate automation. Valid optional parameters must not break recognition. Experimental x- names require consenting parties; registration rules need successor review.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: Address forgery, reflection, loops, address enumeration, activity disclosure and responder resource exhaustion remain threats. Header labels alone do not solve them.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 3028
sections.audit: Changes remove test-side-effect ban and reject extension; reconcile modern base behavior rather than inheriting RFC3028 assumptions.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: Applies only when the script requires variables; requirement declarations themselves are not expanded.

sections.title: Capability Identifier
sections.audit: The variables capability denotes interpreter support, not recipient support for Email Next.

sections.title: Interpretation of Strings
sections.audit: Expansion is single-pass, names are case-insensitive, unknown variables become empty; namespace use requires the relevant extension.

sections.title: Quoting and Encoded Characters
sections.audit: Backslash decoding precedes encoded-character decoding and then variable substitution; a backslash does not generally prevent expansion.

sections.title: Match Variables
sections.audit: Successful non-greedy matches populate numbered captures; evaluation short-circuits left-to-right; list iteration order is not fully fixed. Verified erratum5015 corrects fileinfo to fileinto.

sections.title: Action set
sections.audit: Set requires a constant valid name, cannot assign match variables, is script-local by default and does not cancel implicit keep.

sections.title: Modifiers
sections.audit: Modifiers run by descending precedence; duplicate precedence and unknown modifiers are errors.

sections.title: Modifier ":length"
sections.audit: Length counts characters, not UTF-8 octets; do not use it as an SMTP SIZE measurement.

sections.title: Modifier ":quotewildcard"
sections.audit: Quotewildcard quotes wildcard syntax only; it is not HTML, JSON, URL or shell escaping.

sections.title: Case Modifiers
sections.audit: Case conversion affects ASCII letters only; not Unicode case folding or mailbox canonicalization.

sections.title: Modifier ":upper"
sections.audit: Upper converts every ASCII lowercase letter.

sections.title: Modifier ":lower"
sections.audit: Lower converts every ASCII uppercase letter.

sections.title: Modifier ":upperfirst"
sections.audit: Upperfirst affects only the first character when it is an ASCII lowercase letter.

sections.title: Modifier ":lowerfirst"
sections.audit: Lowerfirst affects only the first character when it is an ASCII uppercase letter.

sections.title: Test string
sections.audit: String compares script-supplied lists without implicit whitespace stripping; relational count ignores empty members.

sections.title: Implementation Limits
sections.audit: Minimum capacities are 128 variables, 32-character names and 4000-character values; runtime overflow must not be an error and should truncate. Unsupported match indexes are syntax errors.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: Sender-controlled captures and truncation make variables unsuitable for security-bearing structures; filtering is not hostile-message authentication.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.audit: Registers variables as a Sieve capability; no new sender-requested discard behavior.

sections.title: Acknowledgments
sections.audit: Acknowledgments reviewed; no additional protocol behavior.

sections.title: References
sections.audit: Both reference lists and end matter reviewed.

sections.title: IANA Considerations

sections.title: SMTP Enhanced Status Codes Registry
sections.audit: Three tables: classes, subjects and enumerated subject/detail pairs. Associated basic status codes are explicitly non-exclusive; unspecified does not mean forbidden. Descriptions and reference status matter.

sections.title: Message Rejection and Bouncing
sections.audit: Reject rather than damage mail. Unknown return route to submitter should reject immediately; null MAIL FROM alone must not cause rejection. Other rejections may be delayed bounces, but immediate feedback preferred; client needs submitted-message correlation.

sections.title: Authorized Submission

sections.audit: Envelope domains must be qualified; examining/modifying text beyond trace triggers qualification duty for address headers. Verified local single-label expansion possible; incomplete multi-level expansion discouraged.

sections.title: Require Authentication
sections.audit: Default MAIL530 without SMTP authentication unless independent authentication/authorization already established.

sections.audit: Illegal envelope/address header syntax should reject; MAIL/RCPT501, post-DATA invalid address554 with suitable detail.

sections.title: Log Errors
sections.audit: Log client errors with limits to prevent logging denial of service.

sections.title: Apply Shorter Timeouts
sections.audit: Submission servers should respond in under2minutes evenDATA; tightly coupled systems may agree shorter timeouts. Timeout is not proof of nonacceptance.

sections.title: Optional Actions

sections.title: Enforce Submission Rights

sections.title: Support for the Postmaster Address

sections.title: Adjust Character Encodings
sections.audit: Charset/string conversion and known out-of-band address substitution allowed subject to other protocols; not arbitrary transliteration or signature preservation guarantee.

sections.title: Interaction with SMTP Extensions

Forged positive/negative reports, parser attacks, blowback and correlation risks reviewed. Message-ID correlation is not authentication.

sections.title: Introduction

sections.title: Overview
sections.audit: Requires metadata, environment and flag support; server processing can benefit intermittently connected clients.

sections.title: Differences between IMAP Events and Mail Delivery
sections.audit: APPEND may lack any delivery envelope or original sender context; bulk user actions can trigger many independent script runs.

sections.title: Conventions Used in This Document
sections.audit: Requirement-keyword conventions reviewed.

sections.title: The "IMAP Events in Sieve" Extension
sections.audit: Defines IMAP-event execution, not authenticated Email Next events.

sections.title: The "imapsieve" Capability Strings
sections.audit: One IMAPSIEVE ManageSieve endpoint is advertised; scripts require imapsieve and directly used environment support explicitly.

sections.title: Existing IMAP Functions Affected by IMAP Events in Sieve
sections.audit: Each affected message triggers separately; execution may be parallel, so no global serial order is supplied.

sections.title: The IMAP APPEND Command
sections.audit: APPEND triggers configured scripts; MULTIAPPEND invokes once per created message.

sections.title: The IMAP COPY Command
sections.audit: COPY triggers scripts on newly created copies under selected metadata.

sections.title: Changes to IMAP Message Flags
sections.audit: Flag changes expose post-change flags; implementations must prevent loops and should suppress recursive flag-triggered invocation.

sections.title: When Script Actions Set the \Deleted Flag
sections.audit: Action-induced Deleted flags do not invoke another script; optional expunge targets only affected messages, not unrelated deletions.

sections.title: New Functions Defined by IMAP Events in Sieve
sections.audit: Metadata supplies script selection.

sections.title: Interaction with Metadata
sections.audit: Mailbox metadata takes precedence over server metadata; an empty, missing-script or unusable mailbox selection does not fall back to the server script. ManageSieve support is required.

sections.title: Applicable Sieve Actions and Interactions
sections.audit: Action semantics depend on this execution context and each extension's interaction rules.

sections.title: The Implicit Keep
sections.audit: Implicit keep preserves the original immutable message; transient content modifications are not retained.

sections.title: The "keep" Action
sections.audit: Explicit keep has the same original-message preservation semantics.

sections.title: The "fileinto" Action
sections.audit: Fileinto creates a separate message and does not trigger another IMAP event; without keep the original is marked Deleted, not silently never stored.

sections.title: The "redirect" Action
sections.audit: Redirect can submit a message with reconstructed envelope/header information; original storage remains and without keep is marked Deleted. Submission fix-up is not preservation of authenticated bytes.

sections.title: The "discard" Action
sections.audit: Discard first stores APPEND/COPY input, then marks Deleted unless explicit keep applies; this is not invisible delivery.

sections.title: The "notify" Action
sections.audit: Notify sends a notification while normal message handling otherwise continues.

sections.title: The "addheader" and "deleteheader" Actions
sections.audit: Header edits are transient for outgoing/new copies and do not mutate a kept message in place.

sections.title: The "setflag", "deleteflag", and "removeflag" Actions
sections.audit: Flag actions and hasflag operate on current flags; recursive execution must be prevented. Heading naming does not substitute for the referenced flag extension's action definitions.

sections.title: MIME Part Tests and Replacement
sections.audit: MIME replacement/enclosure is transient and cannot rewrite the kept immutable original.

sections.title: spamtest and virustest
sections.audit: Spam and virus tests may apply; their results are not endpoint identity evidence.

sections.title: Inapplicable Actions
sections.audit: Reject, ereject and vacation requirements or use terminate an IMAP-event script with an error.

sections.title: Future Sieve Actions
sections.audit: Future action extensions must specify IMAP-event applicability; delivery-only actions remain inapplicable.

sections.title: Interaction with Sieve Environment
sections.audit: Environment describes invocation context, not authenticated message authorship.

sections.title: Base Sieve Environment Items: location and phase
sections.audit: Location is MS and phase is post, including APPEND that may replace delivery entirely.

sections.title: New Sieve Environment Items: imap.user and imap.email
sections.audit: imap.user and imap.email identify the acting IMAP user; both are empty during normal final delivery.

sections.title: New Sieve Environment Item: imap.cause
sections.audit: APPEND, COPY and FLAG identify causes; future causes require requested extension capabilities.

sections.title: New Sieve Environment Item: imap.mailbox
sections.audit: Mailbox name is fixed at invocation and is not changed by fileinto.

sections.title: New Sieve Environment Item: imap.changedflags
sections.audit: Changedflags lists changed names, not set/reset direction; inspect current flags for direction. Other causes yield empty text.

sections.title: Interaction with Sieve Tests (Comparisons)
sections.audit: Envelope tests are forbidden and generate runtime errors outside final delivery; other comparisons are unchanged.

sections.title: Examples
sections.audit: All three examples reviewed: copy-based redirect, changed-flag notification and post-TLS capability discovery; none proves authenticated receipt.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: Prevent flag, redirect and notify loops; fileinto does not recursively invoke scripts. Innocuous flag changes can leak appended plaintext drafts through redirect.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.audit: Capability, environment and metadata registrations reviewed; current registry checks remain separate.

sections.audit: Prefer SMTP extension. Header MUST NOT be used without specific knowledge of processing support and SHOULD NOT be used for multiple recipients; it leaks relationships and lacks hop assurance.

sections.title: Handling By Receivers
sections.audit: Envelope parameter takes precedence for its recipient. Temporary lookup errors use transient failure. Missing historical data permits a justified latest-possible substitute; absent a reasonable substitute reject.

sections.title: SMTP Extension Used
sections.audit: Known role accounts are exempt. Negative continuous-ownership check rejects RCPT with550 before delivery.

sections.title: Relays
sections.audit: Relays preserve action. Unsupported next hop with default/R requires rejection: synchronous DATA550 or DSN and stop. Do not silently convert strict protection.

sections.title: Header Field Used
sections.audit: Only valid, locally handled, current-envelope matching header targets without corresponding RRVS are checked; role accounts excluded. Recommended removal at local delivery, or removal of applicable checked fields when forwarding.

sections.title: Design Choices
sections.audit: Forwarding controlled by same owner can satisfy original check; remaining original-address header is inapplicable at new mailbox. Header and envelope need not otherwise match.

sections.title: Clock Synchronization
sections.audit: Both parties must synchronize clocks using a standard protocol; clock error can misclassify ownership.

sections.title: Relaying without RRVS Support
sections.audit: Failure is preferred for unsupported onward relay. Header downgrade or dropping requires the permissive action and careful risk knowledge; not an override of5.1.1.

sections.title: Header Field Conversion
sections.audit: Header-to-extension conversion SHOULD remove header; reverse conversion requires rejection declined and prior knowledge of downstream processing, plus privacy restrictions.

sections.title: Header Field with Multiple Recipients
sections.audit: One failed header check can fail all recipients at DATA; acceptance followed by per-recipient DSNs is alternative. Forwarding convergence and timestamp fanout are privacy/diagnostic hazards.

sections.title: Special Use Addresses
sections.audit: Special address handlers SHOULD NOT invent RRVS when absent inbound.

sections.title: Mailing Lists

sections.title: Single-Recipient Aliases

sections.title: Multiple-Recipient Aliases

sections.title: Confidential Forwarding Addresses

sections.title: Continuous Ownership

sections.title: Conventions Used in This Document
sections.audit: Reference identifiers are expected service identities. DNS-ID, SRV-ID, URI-ID and historical CN-ID are distinct certificate identifier types.

sections.title: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
sections.audit: Validate the certificate path before service-name matching. Reference names come from configured email domain, connection hostname without CNAME canonicalization, or securely derived names. DNS-ID support is required; RFC6186 discovery also requires SRV-ID support and an email-domain reference. URI-ID is prohibited here. Historical CN-ID fallback is optional. Wildcards occupy the whole leftmost label, not a fragment. Reconcile with the successor to RFC6125 before selecting a modern profile.

sections.title: Compliance Checklist for Certification Authorities
sections.audit: CA checklist requires DNS-ID and email SRV-ID issuance support and historical CN-ID compatibility; leftmost wildcard issuance is optional. These are source requirements, not evidence of actual CA support.

sections.title: Notes on Handling of Delegated Email Services by Certification
sections.audit: Delegated service authorization must cover every requested domain. A CA unable to verify that authority must not issue the email service identifiers. DNSSEC and certificates binding the original service domain are possible delegation evidence; plain redirection alone is insufficient.

sections.title: Compliance Checklist for Mail Service Providers and Certificate
sections.audit: CSR guidance includes service host DNS-IDs, recommends email-domain DNS-IDs, and requires applicable SRV-IDs for RFC6186 discovery. Historical CN and wildcard guidance is recorded without making it the new profile.

sections.title: Notes on Hosting Multiple Domains
sections.audit: Multiple-domain strategies include pinned or DNSSEC-authenticated delegation, multi-name certificates, separate endpoints and SNI. Each has operational costs. SNI selects a certificate; it does not itself authorize the delegation. The RFC leaves large-scale hosting issues unresolved.

sections.title: Examples

Preserve local-part case and meaningful syntax equivalence; no inferred subaddress equivalence. Subset requests need separate envelope copies. Multiple clients need coordination.

sections.title: The Disposition-Notification-Options Header

sections.title: Format of a Message Disposition Notification
sections.audit: Multipart/report with readable explanation, machine part and optional returned source. Returned encrypted content stays encrypted. DNT destination in both envelope/header, null sender, distinct report Message-ID.

sections.title: The Message/Disposition-Notification Media Type
sections.audit: ASCII 7bit machine part; no parameters. Field order recommended, not fixed; extensions may appear anywhere. Restriction does not apply to optional returned original.

sections.title: General Conventions for Fields
sections.audit: Case-insensitive names, folding and grammar-appropriate comments; encoded words only where comment syntax permits.

sections.title: Original-Recipient Field

sections.title: Final-Recipient Field

sections.title: Original-Message-ID Field

sections.title: Disposition Field

sections.title: Disposition Modes

sections.title: Disposition Types
sections.audit: Displayed not read or understood; processed may be automated; dispatched may be printed/forwarded; deleted may already have been seen and may be restored.

sections.title: Disposition Modifiers
sections.audit: Unknown modifiers may be ignored or shown without interpretation, never produce an error response. One report per recipient/message, with forwarding considerations.

sections.title: Error Field

sections.title: Extension-Fields
sections.audit: Extension fields require registration; foreign and implementation-specific diagnostics must not acquire endpoint authority.

sections.title: Timeline of Events
sections.audit: Remember report issuance; later actions do not generate a continuing activity stream.

sections.title: Conformance and Usage Requirements
sections.audit: No invented original recipient from ordinary SMTP. Alias expansion can yield multiple reports. List processed receipt differs from member receipt; propagation risks subscriber disclosure.

sections.title: Forgery

sections.title: Privacy

sections.title: Disclosure of Product Information

sections.title: MUA Fingerprinting

sections.title: Non-repudiation

sections.title: Mail Bombing

sections.title: Gatewaying from MDNs to Other Mail Systems

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: Submission/access confidentiality, implicit TLS preference and cleartext deprecation; excludes relay transport and explicitly does not replace end-to-end encryption.

sections.title: How This Document Updates Previous RFCs
sections.audit: Updates POP, IMAP, submission, older TLS guidance and SRV configuration; apply8997 to historical version thresholds.

sections.title: Conventions and Terminology Used in This Document
sections.audit: Implicit TLS, account, provider and configuration terms reviewed; ABNF and requirement vocabulary defined.

sections.title: Implicit TLS
sections.audit: Prefer TLS immediately on connection for client/provider services; this is not an SMTP relay-port change.

sections.title: Implicit TLS for POP
sections.audit: POP3S port995 begins TLS immediately; after greeting both peers enter AUTHORIZATION even with a client certificate.

sections.title: Implicit TLS for IMAP
sections.audit: IMAPS port993 begins TLS immediately; acceptable client certificate may lead to PREAUTH, otherwise OK enters NOT AUTHENTICATED.

sections.title: Implicit TLS for SMTP Submission
sections.audit: Submissions port465 begins TLS immediately and retains MSA authentication requirements.587 STARTTLS remains a transition mechanism; correctly required TLS has comparable security properties. No fixed new sunset date is inferred.

sections.title: Implicit TLS Connection Closure for POP, IMAP, and SMTP Submission
sections.audit: Prefer TLS close alerts before TCP termination; client may close after sending its alert without waiting for the peer alert.

sections.title: Use of TLS by Mail Access Servers and Message Submission Servers
sections.audit: Providers support TLS, prefer implicit TLS, advertise usable services, migrate cleartext users, support1.2+, record cipher information and apply current cipher guidance. Apply8997 to obsolete1.1 migration language.

sections.title: Deprecation of Services Using Cleartext and TLS Versions
sections.audit: After cleartext access revocation, valid and invalid credentials receive the same denial; avoid a credential-validity oracle. Consider rotation of exposed passwords. Apply8997 version updates.

sections.title: Mail Server Use of Client Certificate Authentication
sections.audit: Request client certificates only when usable for account authentication; accepted authorization enables SASL EXTERNAL, with IMAPS PREAUTH alternative.

sections.title: Recording TLS Ciphersuite in "Received" Header Field
sections.audit: Received tls clause records registered cipher name or0x plus four hex digits; optional group follows immediately. Trace text is not end-to-end authentication or proof of every hop.

sections.title: TLS Server Certificate Requirements
sections.audit: Maintain valid service certificates; multiple-domain deployments use appropriate certificates/endpoints/SNI and support post-SRV hostname interoperability.

sections.title: Recommended DNS Records for Mail Protocol Servers
sections.audit: DNS guidance covers discovery and trust configuration, not recipient device capabilities.

sections.title: MX Records
sections.audit: MX and DNSSEC recommendation concerns inbound delivery; relay handling remains outside this document.

sections.title: SRV Records
sections.audit: Advertise SRV and prefer implicit TLS over cleartext or STARTTLS.

sections.title: DNSSEC
sections.audit: Sign service-discovery DNS records when the parent zone supports DNSSEC.

sections.title: TLSA Records
sections.audit: TLSA advertisement is recommended as additional trust evidence but forbidden here without DNSSEC signing.

sections.title: Changes to Internet-Facing Servers
sections.audit: Replacing public-facing servers, including filters, generally preserves or improves supported TLS version.

sections.title: Use of TLS by Mail User Agents
sections.audit: Clients support discovery, per-account minimum protection, validated certificates and accurate indicators. Apply8997 version thresholds; detect upgrades for legacy accounts without silently weakening protected ones.

sections.title: Use of SRV Records in Establishing Configuration
sections.audit: Adds _submissions._tcp; filter services below minimum protection before ranking. Credential testing must respect the minimum; insecure setup requires explicit warning. Do not rediscover on every connection without validated DNSSEC. Periodic change detection is allowed.

sections.title: Minimum Confidentiality Level
sections.audit: Default per-account protection validates certificates;8997 raises recommended version to1.2. Until minimum is met allow only capability discovery or STARTTLS. Avoid routine click-through bypass. Explicit reconfiguration is distinct from transient connection failure.

sections.title: Certificate Validation
sections.audit: Validate using7817 and PKIX; DANE is optional. Exception pinning alone does not satisfy the specified minimum confidentiality.

sections.title: Certificate Pinning
sections.audit: Exception pinning is setup-only, account-scoped and revocable; not offered on validation failure for an existing account. Distinguish this from authenticated key continuity and HTTP pinning.

sections.title: Client Certificate Authentication
sections.audit: Client certificates require account-specific authorization and a server request. Installing one for another account is not permission to disclose it. Supporting clients implement SASL EXTERNAL.

sections.title: Considerations Related to Antivirus/Antispam Software and Services
sections.audit: Intermediary scanners must meet the same transport requirements. End-to-end encryption limits server-side content scanning; this does not authorize decryption or silent fallback.

Two opposite mechanisms: REQUIRETLS requires authenticated protected relay; TLS-Required:No requests relaxing recipient transport policy. Neither is end-to-end encryption.
Requirement vocabulary and ABNF reviewed.

Argument-free REQUIRETLS EHLO and MAIL parameter; adds11 octets; applies relay/submission/LMTP. Requires TLS, authenticated MX via DNSSEC orMTA-STS, validated certificate viaPKIX orDANE, and fresh postTLS capability.
Only TLS-Required:No is defined, at most once. Requests best-effort delivery despite recipient policy, while still preferring available STARTTLS. No Yes header equivalent exists.
Message tagging propagates selected transport handling.
MAIL REQUIRETLS overrides a conflicting header. Alias redistribution tags all resulting instances identically.
Distinguishes required and optional transport paths.

Authenticate routing and TLS, require postTLS capability, try remaining MX hosts on failure, otherwise fail without transmitting. Reports5.7.30 or5.7.10. Reported7705 identifies DANE/name-check tension; unresolved pending DANE audit, not silently accepted.
TLS-Required:No requests trying delivery despite unsuccessful policy/TLS checks, but cannot force a server to accept without TLS. Unsupported hops need not honor it uniformly.
Originator policy may select requirement without per-message prompting. Requirement uses SMTP negotiation; optional override uses header. Neither implies recipient device support.
Access/delivery agents should follow8314; relay requirement alone does not prove protected end-user access.

Bounces generally inherit REQUIRETLS and suppress original body as RET=HDRS even if RET=FULL requested. Empty-return-path bounce exception says lack of downstream REQUIRETLS should not itself cause discard; lost reports and metadata leakage remain possible.
Reoriginators should preserve requirements to extent feasible; user-side mediators may lack envelope policy. No universal propagation guarantee or permission to decrypt.
Registers REQUIRETLS, TLS-Required andX.7.30; status code checked in preceding live registry review.
Threat model separates network protection from compromised relays.
Passive resistance depends on actual TLS security.
Required TLS resists stripping and certificate substitution; MX authentication resists redirection to a valid attacker certificate.
Malicious relays can lie or strip requirements; content remains visible absent end-to-end encryption.
Optional override can ignore advertised DANE/MTA-STS policy, but server enforcement remains decisive. Rejected8593 does not restrict mechanism to misconfiguration reports only.
References reviewed; general TLS/DNSSEC/DANE/MTA-STS/DSN dependencies remain open.
Previously reviewed SMTP,STARTTLS,message format and8314 are not dependency closure. Historical6125/7525 require successor reconciliation.
Mediator,access,submission and content-encryption references do not specify complete Email Next behavior.

sections.title: Envelope Structure Message Attribute

sections.audit: Selective retrieval is useful; parsed structure and partial bytes do not establish cryptographic validity.

sections.title: 8-Bit and Binary Strings
sections.audit: Literal lengths count octets; even an empty synchronizing literal needs continuation. NUL requires the permitted binary form.

sections.audit: Preserve nesting and the distinction between NIL, empty values and an atom naming a mailbox NIL.

sections.title: Mailbox Naming
sections.audit: Mailbox NFC and case rules do not authorize normalization of signed message bytes or identities. INBOX is a special case.

sections.title: Mailbox Hierarchy Naming

sections.title: Namespaces

sections.title: Historic Mailbox Namespace Naming Convention
sections.audit: Prefixes and accessibility depend on the server and authenticated account; access is not conversation membership.

sections.title: Common Namespace Models
sections.audit: Prefixes and accessibility depend on the server and authenticated account; access is not conversation membership.

sections.title: Mailbox Size and Message Status Updates
sections.audit: Remember message and flag changes; EXISTS cannot reduce the message count.

sections.title: Response When No Command in Progress
sections.audit: Respect flow and expunge restrictions rather than assuming responses belong to the last command.

sections.title: Autologout Timer
sections.audit: The protocol's idle timing is not a presence signal or an Email Next policy default.

sections.title: Multiple Commands in Progress (Command Pipelining)
sections.audit: Sequence-number changes and saved-search dependencies constrain safe concurrency.

sections.title: Client Commands
sections.audit: BAD and NO have different semantics; failed SELECT/EXAMINE can still change selection state.

sections.title: Client Commands - Any State
sections.audit: Advertising a feature is not enabling it. A dual rev1/rev2 server initially retains rev1 behavior.

sections.title: CAPABILITY Command
sections.audit: Advertising a feature is not enabling it. A dual rev1/rev2 server initially retains rev1 behavior.

sections.title: NOOP Command
sections.audit: Polls account state, not peer presence or human reading.

sections.title: LOGOUT Command
sections.audit: Process BYE and the tagged completion in their specified order.

sections.title: Client Commands - Not Authenticated State
sections.audit: TLS does not itself authenticate an account or grant message privileges.

sections.title: STARTTLS Command
sections.audit: Discard pre-TLS capabilities and prevent buffered plaintext from becoming post-TLS commands.

sections.title: AUTHENTICATE Command
sections.audit: Apply SASL framing, cancellation and security-layer boundaries; refresh capabilities after a changed security context.

sections.title: LOGIN Command
sections.audit: Do not expose passwords on an unprotected connection or ignore LOGINDISABLED.

sections.title: Client Commands - Authenticated State
sections.audit: Mailbox operations remain constrained by account permissions.

sections.title: ENABLE Command
sections.audit: Enablement is additive and acknowledged by ENABLED; unknown or inapplicable requests are ignored, not inferred successful.

sections.title: Note to Designers of Extensions That May Use the ENABLE
sections.audit: Use ENABLE only when incompatible response behavior requires it.

sections.title: SELECT Command
sections.audit: Retain required mailbox metadata; selecting a new mailbox first closes the old one, including on failure.

sections.title: EXAMINE Command
sections.audit: Read-only examination forbids permanent changes, including per-user state.

sections.title: CREATE Command
sections.audit: Normalize consistently or reject; reusing a name must not silently reuse old UID identity.

sections.title: DELETE Command
sections.audit: Successful deletion removes messages but must not recursively delete child mailboxes.

sections.title: RENAME Command
sections.audit: Children normally follow the rename; INBOX has special behavior. Subscriptions do not automatically follow.

sections.title: SUBSCRIBE Command
sections.audit: Idempotent account preferences, potentially naming nonexistent mailboxes; not conversation membership or permissions.

sections.title: UNSUBSCRIBE Command
sections.audit: Idempotent account preferences, potentially naming nonexistent mailboxes; not conversation membership or permissions.

sections.title: LIST Command
sections.audit: Options, wildcard and reference semantics matter. A listing is not necessarily a complete inventory of accessible mailboxes.

sections.title: LIST Selection Options
sections.audit: SUBSCRIBED may include nonexistent names; REMOTE expands scope; RECURSIVEMATCH requires a base selection option.

sections.title: LIST Return Options
sections.audit: Extra returned data does not expand the selection. Missing STATUS data must not be interpreted as zero.

sections.title: General Principles for Returning LIST Responses
sections.audit: At most one solicited LIST response per name; account for selection and descendant rules.

sections.title: Additional LIST-Related Requirements on Clients
sections.audit: NonExistent implies NoSelect; NoInferiors implies HasNoChildren.

sections.title: The CHILDREN Return Option
sections.audit: HasNoChildren concerns accessible children; NoInferiors additionally forbids future children. Listings can race with changes.

sections.title: CHILDINFO Extended Data Item
sections.audit: Describes descendant selection matches, not proof that a usable child mailbox exists.

sections.title: OLDNAME Extended Data Item
sections.audit: Correlates normalization, rename or deletion; does not authenticate a new principal.

sections.title: LIST Command Examples
sections.audit: Selection and return options differ; child information can describe nonexistent subscriptions. Multi-pattern examples need LIST-EXTENDED beyond the base grammar.

sections.title: NAMESPACE Command
sections.audit: Accept multiple namespaces and account-specific visibility; source examples need the corrections discussed below.

sections.title: STATUS Command
sections.audit: Does not select or mutate the mailbox. Do not use it to poll the selected mailbox; SIZE may be expensive and is an upper bound.

sections.title: APPEND Command
sections.audit: Storage is not delivery. Failure rolls back the append, with a possible UIDNEXT change; write-only access must not expose APPENDUID.

sections.title: IDLE Command
sections.audit: Receives mailbox updates until DONE; no new command during continuation. Unsolicited FETCH includes UID. Not peer presence.

sections.title: Client Commands - Selected State
sections.audit: Message mutation requires a selected mailbox and applicable access rights.

sections.title: CLOSE Command
sections.audit: Expunges deleted messages on a writable mailbox; it is not a harmless deselection operation.

sections.title: UNSELECT Command
sections.audit: Deselects without expunging.

sections.title: EXPUNGE Command
sections.audit: Removes all messages flagged deleted in the mailbox; concurrent clients make blanket expunge consequential.

sections.title: SEARCH Command
sections.audit: Search narrows candidates. HEADER substring results still need exact local parsing and verification; BODY/TEXT may use flexible matching.

sections.title: SAVE Result Option and SEARCH Result Variable
sections.audit: SAVE sets a connection-local message set. Selection, UIDVALIDITY and expunge affect it; MIN/MAX alone save only extrema.

sections.title: Multiple Commands in Progress
sections.audit: Execute a saved search before commands consuming its result, even when pipelined.

sections.title: Refusing to Save Search Results
sections.audit: NOTSAVED clears the result; never reuse an older set after failure.

sections.title: Examples Showing Use of the SAVE Result Option
sections.audit: Test option combinations and failure paths; the verified BADCHARSET correction itself has a semantic inconsistency.

sections.title: FETCH Command
sections.audit: Prefer PEEK for background processing. BINARY offsets address decoded content; BODY offsets address the transmitted representation.

sections.title: FETCH Section Specification
sections.audit: MIME part numbering and header subsetting have exact rules; selected headers are not a substitute for the protected entity.

sections.title: STORE Command
sections.audit: Changes flags, not immutable message bytes. SILENT does not suppress unrelated flag updates.

sections.title: COPY Command
sections.audit: Preserves content with a new mailbox identity; failure must roll back the destination copy, apart from possible UIDNEXT increments.

sections.title: MOVE Command
sections.audit: A set can partially succeed. Each message remains in at least one mailbox; map COPYUID before EXPUNGE and reconcile duplicates.

sections.title: UID Command
sections.audit: Missing UIDs can yield successful no-ops. FETCH/EXPUNGE leading numbers remain sequence numbers; UID EXPUNGE narrows deletion.

sections.title: Client Commands - Experimental/Expansion
sections.audit: New commands need capabilities; new untagged responses require the associated command or enablement. No silent legacy behavior is implied.

sections.title: Server Responses
sections.audit: Process state updates independently of command completion, subject to connection-state security rules.

sections.title: Server Responses - Generic Status Responses
sections.audit: Use machine-readable codes; unknown codes are ignored. Protect sensitive UID information and distrust unprotected ALERT text.

sections.title: OK Response
sections.audit: Untagged information is not command completion.

sections.title: NO Response
sections.audit: Untagged warnings can accompany a successful command; tagged NO is the operation result.

sections.title: BAD Response
sections.audit: Distinguish protocol errors and untagged server failures.

sections.title: PREAUTH Response
sections.audit: On an unprotected port it prevents STARTTLS; mandatory-TLS clients must close.

sections.title: BYE Response
sections.audit: Read pending responses through closure; normal logout and immediate failure differ.

sections.title: Server Responses - Server Status
sections.audit: The acknowledged list, possibly empty, identifies enabled features.

sections.title: ENABLED Response
sections.audit: The acknowledged list, possibly empty, identifies enabled features.

sections.title: CAPABILITY Response
sections.audit: Capabilities can change after TLS or authentication. Unknown names do not authorize guessed behavior.

sections.title: Server Responses - Mailbox Status
sections.audit: Special-use roles are optional, account-specific and potentially repeated; an All mailbox may omit Trash/Junk.

sections.title: LIST Response
sections.audit: Special-use roles are optional, account-specific and potentially repeated; an All mailbox may omit Trash/Junk.

sections.title: NAMESPACE Response
sections.audit: Missing namespace classes use NIL; extensions require tolerant structural parsing.

sections.title: STATUS Response
sections.audit: Associate returned data with the named mailbox, not the selected mailbox by assumption.

sections.title: ESEARCH Response
sections.audit: Honor the correlator and UID indicator; result order is unspecified and returned ranges must be complete.

sections.title: FLAGS Response
sections.audit: Remember available flags, separately from PERMANENTFLAGS.

sections.title: Server Responses - Mailbox Size
sections.audit: Remember counts; presence of a new message does not prove a new conversation event.

sections.title: EXISTS Response
sections.audit: Remember counts; presence of a new message does not prove a new conversation event.

sections.title: Server Responses - Message Status
sections.audit: Renumber immediately; UID commands have different expunge interleaving rules from plain FETCH/STORE/SEARCH.

sections.title: EXPUNGE Response
sections.audit: Renumber immediately; UID commands have different expunge interleaving rules from plain FETCH/STORE/SEARCH.

sections.title: FETCH Response
sections.audit: ENVELOPE defaults and BODYSTRUCTURE decoding lose original representation detail. BINARY normalizes text line endings. Fetch verification inputs deliberately.

sections.title: Server Responses - Command Continuation Request
sections.audit: Wait before sending synchronizing literal bytes; the remaining command follows the counted bytes.

sections.title: Sample IMAP4rev2 Connection
sections.audit: Illustrative exchange, not a ready-made conformance fixture; reconcile omissions against normative requirements.

sections.title: Formal Syntax
sections.audit: Exact spaces, literal lengths, UTF-8, numeric domains and context matter. Prose/grammar discrepancies remain identified below.

sections.title: Author's Note
sections.audit: Explains lineage; does not import all superseded behavior.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: Protect the access connection independently of end-to-end message protection.

sections.title: TLS-Related Security Considerations
sections.audit: Validate server identity and negotiated protection. Resolve current TLS dependencies before implementing historical algorithm references.

sections.title: STARTTLS Command versus Use of Implicit TLS Port
sections.audit: Both client negotiation paths and server implicit TLS have defined requirements; discovery may override default connection attempts.

sections.title: Client Handling of Unsolicited Responses Not Suitable for the
sections.audit: Ignore mailbox data in inappropriate states and unprotected alerts; account for PREAUTH downgrade hazards.

sections.title: COPYUID and APPENDUID Response Codes
sections.audit: Apply the stricter command-section prohibition on revealing APPENDUID/COPYUID to write-only users.

sections.title: LIST Command and Other Users' Namespace
sections.audit: Do not enumerate users without granted listing access.

sections.title: Use of MD5
sections.audit: Exposing Content-MD5 does not make it a secure authentication mechanism.

sections.title: Other Security Considerations
sections.audit: Avoid credential enumeration, plaintext exposure and unbounded guessing; password policy remains an account service responsibility.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.audit: Existing IMAP TCP services and reserved UDP ports are not new Email Next transports.

sections.title: Updates to IMAP Capabilities Registry
sections.audit: Follow the actual registration procedure, rather than copying fictitious X-prefixed examples.

sections.title: GSSAPI/SASL Service Name
sections.audit: Reuse the registered imap service in its defined role.

sections.title: LIST Selection Options, LIST Return Options, and LIST Extended
sections.audit: Selection, return and extended-data registrations retain RFC5258 procedures.

sections.title: IMAP Mailbox Name Attributes and IMAP Response Codes
sections.audit: Reuse existing meanings; new semantics need their own defined extension.

sections.title: References
sections.audit: References were read as dependencies; their listing is not a full audit of their bodies.

sections.title: Normative References
sections.audit: References were read as dependencies; their listing is not a full audit of their bodies.

sections.title: Informative References
sections.audit: QRESYNC, OBJECTID, ACL and discovery documents remain separate capabilities and review dependencies.

sections.title: Related Protocols
sections.audit: QRESYNC, OBJECTID, ACL and discovery documents remain separate capabilities and review dependencies.

sections.title: Historical Aspects of IMAP and Related Protocols
sections.audit: Older protocol references explain compatibility, not current security defaults.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility with IMAP4rev1
sections.audit: Explicitly enable rev2 on dual servers. Modified UTF-7 belongs to the legacy mailbox interface and has strict shift/case rules.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility with BINARY Extension
sections.audit: Base rev2 includes retrieval only; binary APPEND requires the separate BINARY capability.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility with LIST-EXTENDED Extension
sections.audit: Multiple patterns require LIST-EXTENDED.

sections.title: 63-Bit Body Part and Message Sizes
sections.audit: Clients must handle 63-bit sizes; old clients may see hidden or replaced oversized messages. Do not claim complete history from such a view.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 3501 / IMAP4rev1
sections.audit: Informative summary contains terminology and spelling issues; normative sections and grammar govern.

sections.title: Other Recommended IMAP Extensions
sections.audit: QRESYNC/CONDSTORE reduce synchronization cost; OBJECTID preserves caches across moves and renames. Neither is required by the base.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 1
sections.audit: Existing reaction semantics, not arbitrary emoji in prose.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 2
sections.audit: Unicode sequence grammar distinct from ABNF; dependency version must be fixed.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 3
sections.audit: text/plain UTF-8, one emoji line, outer body or first multipart part. Invalid candidates may be handled individually; unsupported code points remain displayable placeholders.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 4
sections.audit: Known In-Reply-To target needed; outer-level processing. Wording permits a wider part search than§3placement; generate firstpart and retain ambiguity for received later parts. Nested messages processed independently.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 5
sections.audit: Audience and repeated-reaction UX unspecified; proposal must define them.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 5.1
sections.audit: Example has invalid date and unbracketed IDs; do not copy into fixtures.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 5.2
sections.audit: Displays explicitly untested; no usability evidence claimed.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 6
sections.audit: Social engineering and special processing risks acknowledged; no authentication supplied.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 7
sections.audit: Reaction is used as disposition type despite parameter wording; current registry verification open.

sections.title: RFC9078 section 8
sections.audit: Experimental goals reviewed; publication does not establish adoption.
