sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: HTTP semantics support service interaction; they do not define email conversation identity.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.audit: Service internals and effects beyond one response remain outside the uniform interface.

sections.title: History and Evolution
sections.audit: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 share semantics; transport upgrades do not prove Email Next capability.

sections.title: Core Semantics
sections.audit: Interpret method, status, fields and content together.

sections.title: Specifications Obsoleted by This Document
sections.audit: Use consolidated semantics rather than importing obsolete predecessor wording unchecked.

sections.title: Conformance
sections.audit: Conformance depends on the HTTP roles implemented.

sections.title: Syntax Notation
sections.audit: ABNF and case-sensitive notation apply; expanded list grammar has distinct sender/recipient rules.

sections.title: Requirements Notation
sections.audit: An endpoint profile cannot redefine existing method semantics or advertise unsupported versions.

sections.title: Length Requirements
sections.audit: Apply defensible implementation limits; no arbitrary universal Email Next size follows from HTTP.

sections.title: Error Handling
sections.audit: Permitted recovery is not a requirement to repair security-sensitive endpoint data.

sections.title: Protocol Version
sections.audit: HTTP version negotiation and application capability negotiation remain separate.

sections.title: Terminology and Core Concepts
sections.audit: Resource, message and intermediary terminology is adopted only for HTTP operations.

sections.title: Resources
sections.audit: A resource URI cannot turn a safe method into answer submission.

sections.title: Representations
sections.audit: A representation describes resource state; it is not the resource or a durable conversation event.

sections.title: Connections, Clients, and Servers
sections.audit: Connection reuse does not establish that two requests come from one principal.

sections.title: Messages
sections.audit: HTTP request/response messages are separate from email contributions.

sections.title: User Agents
sections.audit: Automated clients and scanners are user agents too; retrieval is not evidence of a click.

sections.title: Origin Server
sections.audit: Origin authority concerns its resource namespace, not a sender's conversation identity.

sections.title: Intermediaries
sections.audit: Proxy, gateway and tunnel trust boundaries remain explicit.

sections.title: Caches
sections.audit: Cached responses can bypass the origin; freshness and authorization require a caching profile.

sections.title: Example Message Exchange
sections.audit: GET example illustrates ordinary retrieval, not an action receipt or secure deployment.

sections.title: Identifiers in HTTP
sections.audit: Endpoint identity requires parsed URI semantics.

sections.title: URI References
sections.audit: Resolve references against defined bases; support and bound URI lengths without truncating targets.

sections.title: HTTP-Related URI Schemes
sections.audit: Scheme presence does not prove a service exists or supports the proposal.

sections.title: http URI Scheme
sections.audit: Plain HTTP authority is insufficient for protected credentials or submission content.

sections.title: https URI Scheme
sections.audit: Require secured HTTPS requests and responses; HTTPS does not hide content from the service.

sections.title: http(s) Normalization and Comparison
sections.audit: Normalization must preserve origin and resource identity; path/query are not generally case-insensitive.

sections.title: Deprecation of userinfo in http(s) URIs
sections.audit: Reject userinfo in message-supplied endpoints to avoid misleading authority and credential leakage.

sections.title: http(s) References with Fragment Identifiers
sections.audit: Fragments are client-side references, not part of the HTTP target.

sections.title: Authoritative Access
sections.audit: Resource authority is distinct from authorization to act in a conversation.

sections.title: URI Origin
sections.audit: Bind scheme, normalized host and port; common ownership does not merge origins.

sections.title: http Origins
sections.audit: DNS/routing-based plain HTTP authority does not provide authenticated service identity.

sections.title: https Origins
sections.audit: Certificate-valid connection reuse still requires correct target-origin routing.

sections.title: https Certificate Verification
sections.audit: Certificate matching uses service identity, not CN-ID; current identity-verification dependencies need reconciliation.

sections.title: IP-ID Reference Identity
sections.audit: IP-literal service identities require exact address bytes in certificate subjectAltName.

sections.title: Fields
sections.audit: Use HTTP field semantics separately from email header semantics.

sections.title: Field Names
sections.audit: Case-insensitive names and unknown-field forwarding do not make new fields universally understood.

sections.title: Field Lines and Combined Field Value
sections.audit: Combine repeated list fields in received order; reported erratum 9162 concerns separator wording.

sections.title: Field Order
sections.audit: Do not blindly combine singleton fields or Set-Cookie; complete headers precede request effects.

sections.title: Field Limits
sections.audit: Reject excessive request fields instead of silently ignoring security-relevant values.

sections.title: Field Values
sections.audit: Control-character and singleton/list ambiguity must not create inconsistent authorization parsing.

sections.title: Common Rules for Defining Field Values
sections.audit: Common grammar rules constrain any new endpoint fields.

sections.title: Lists (#rule ABNF Extension)
sections.audit: List notation distinguishes generated syntax from tolerant receipt.

sections.title: Sender Requirements
sections.audit: Senders do not generate empty list elements.

sections.title: Recipient Requirements
sections.audit: Recipients tolerate reasonable empty elements without accepting empty required lists or unbounded work.

sections.title: Tokens
sections.audit: Token character sets constrain names and unquoted values.

sections.title: Whitespace
sections.audit: Interpret optional, required and historical whitespace per grammar.

sections.title: Quoted Strings
sections.audit: Quoted-pair unescaping applies only where that production is defined.

sections.title: Comments
sections.audit: Comments are legal only where explicitly allowed; do not import email comment syntax everywhere.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.audit: Parameter names are case-insensitive; values follow their own definitions; no whitespace around equals.

sections.title: Date/Time Formats
sections.audit: Emit IMF-fixdate and accept defined historical formats; dates are not trusted causal timestamps.

sections.title: Message Abstraction
sections.audit: Keep HTTP framing, metadata and application event bytes separate.

sections.title: Framing and Completeness
sections.audit: Framing completeness is not application acknowledgement; close-delimited responses can be ambiguous.

sections.title: Control Data
sections.audit: Control data and version rules survive translation between HTTP versions.

sections.title: Header Fields
sections.audit: Headers affect routing and interpretation before content processing.

sections.title: Content
sections.audit: Content excludes transfer framing and trailers.

sections.title: Content Semantics
sections.audit: Interpret content using method/status, including content-free response cases.

sections.title: Identifying Content
sections.audit: Content-Location assertions do not independently authenticate a foreign resource.

sections.title: Trailer Fields
sections.audit: Trailers remain separate from headers and cannot retroactively authorize earlier processing.

sections.title: Limitations on Use of Trailers
sections.audit: Essential acknowledgement must not depend solely on trailers surviving intermediaries.

sections.title: Processing Trailer Fields
sections.audit: Declared trailer names neither guarantee arrival nor permit arbitrary header merging.

sections.title: Message Metadata
sections.audit: Message metadata is not conversation event metadata.

sections.title: Date
sections.audit: Intermediaries can add or repair Date; it is not cryptographic proof of action time.

sections.title: Trailer
sections.audit: Trailer advertises expected metadata without guaranteeing it will be sent.

sections.title: Routing HTTP Messages
sections.audit: Bind the actual routed target to the service the user authorized.

sections.title: Determining the Target Resource
sections.audit: Resolve target URI and exclude fragment; fragment-held credentials require a separate client mechanism.

sections.title: Host and :authority
sections.audit: Host or :authority must match the intended target, including port.

sections.title: Routing Inbound Requests
sections.audit: Cache, proxy and direct-origin paths have different trust and availability properties.

sections.title: To a Cache
sections.audit: A cache hit is not evidence the service processed a new request.

sections.title: To a Proxy
sections.audit: Proxy configuration does not authorize disclosure of mailbox credentials to the endpoint.

sections.title: To the Origin
sections.audit: Direct access still requires scheme-specific authority checks.

sections.title: Rejecting Misdirected Requests
sections.audit: Reject misdirected HTTPS requests even when a shared server holds a valid certificate.

sections.title: Response Correlation
sections.audit: Responses can arrive before request completion; transport correlation is not durable submission identity.

sections.title: Message Forwarding
sections.audit: Forwarding can buffer data; no real-time delivery guarantee follows from streaming syntax.

sections.title: Connection
sections.audit: Hop-by-hop fields are removed; essential application semantics cannot depend on them being forwarded.

sections.title: Max-Forwards
sections.audit: Max-Forwards applies to TRACE/OPTIONS diagnostics, not submission replay limits.

sections.title: Via
sections.audit: Via records intermediaries and can use pseudonyms; it does not authenticate conversation authors.

sections.title: Message Transformations
sections.audit: no-transform constrains compliant proxies but is not a cryptographic integrity guarantee.

sections.title: Upgrade
sections.audit: Upgrade changes protocol on one connection, not the underlying transport; preserve outstanding request semantics.

sections.title: Representation Data and Metadata
sections.audit: Define which encoded or decoded bytes the application authenticates.

sections.title: Representation Data
sections.audit: Content-Type then Content-Encoding form the representation encoding model.

sections.title: Representation Metadata
sections.audit: Metadata on HEAD describes the hypothetical GET representation.

sections.title: Content-Type
sections.audit: Do not rely on MIME sniffing or conflicting Content-Type recovery for actionable payloads.

sections.title: Media Type
sections.audit: Media type and parameter semantics require explicit endpoint formats.

sections.title: Charset
sections.audit: Verified erratum 7419 substitutes Accept-Charset for the mistaken Accept-Encoding reference.

sections.title: Multipart Types
sections.audit: Multipart boundary syntax does not delimit the enclosing HTTP message.

sections.title: Content-Encoding
sections.audit: Content codings are representation properties; decoded bytes differ from coded transfer content.

sections.title: Content Codings
sections.audit: Supported content codings require explicit decoding and resource limits.

sections.title: Compress Coding
sections.audit: Legacy compress aliases do not imply required adoption by Email Next.

sections.title: Deflate Coding
sections.audit: Deflate includes a zlib wrapper; raw-deflate compatibility must not be assumed.

sections.title: Gzip Coding
sections.audit: Gzip CRC is not sender authentication or cryptographic integrity.

sections.title: Content-Language
sections.audit: Content-Language describes intended linguistic audience, not authorized recipients.

sections.title: Language Tags
sections.audit: Language tags are distinct from content format and principal identity.

sections.title: Content-Length
sections.audit: Validate lengths, overflow and duplicate values; incorrect framing can enable request smuggling.

sections.title: Content-Location
sections.audit: A receipt URL can identify a report; foreign Content-Location ownership needs independent verification.

sections.title: Validator Fields
sections.audit: HTTP validators support state comparisons, not authenticated contribution identity.

sections.title: Weak versus Strong
sections.audit: Strong validators are resource-scoped; weak validators do not prove byte equality.

sections.title: Last-Modified
sections.audit: Last-Modified reports origin belief about representation change time.

sections.title: Generation
sections.audit: Future dates are constrained and absent clocks limit generation.

sections.title: Comparison
sections.audit: A date validator is usually weak; strength requires the stated timing evidence.

sections.title: ETag
sections.audit: ETag is opaque and may appear in trailers; it is not a mandatory cryptographic digest.

sections.title: Generation
sections.audit: Generation is server-defined; do not infer hashing or globally unique identity.

sections.title: Comparison
sections.audit: Strong and weak comparison have different admissible matches.

sections.title: Example: Entity Tags Varying on Content-Negotiated Resources
sections.audit: Encoded and unencoded representations need different strong tags; transfer coding alone does not.

sections.title: Methods
sections.audit: Existing method semantics constrain endpoint design.

sections.title: Overview
sections.audit: Method tokens are case-sensitive; 405 and 501 distinguish resource support from server implementation.

sections.title: Common Method Properties
sections.audit: Safety, idempotency and cacheability are separate properties.

sections.title: Safe Methods
sections.audit: GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE must not submit an answer merely because a scanner followed a URL.

sections.title: Idempotent Methods
sections.audit: POST retries need known application idempotency or evidence no application occurred.

sections.title: Methods and Caching
sections.audit: POST is not inherently uncachable; response caching rules must be explicit.

sections.title: Method Definitions
sections.audit: Choose methods according to resource semantics rather than visual control labels.

sections.title: GET
sections.audit: GET retrieves; request-body private agreements are not a portable submission mechanism.

sections.title: HEAD
sections.audit: HEAD retrieves metadata without response content; missing generated headers need not indicate no support.

sections.title: POST
sections.audit: POST fits service-specific answer processing; cached POST responses cannot satisfy later POST actions.

sections.title: PUT
sections.audit: PUT creates/replaces known resource state; transformations constrain returned validators.

sections.title: DELETE
sections.audit: DELETE removes URI association, not guaranteed physical erasure or recalled recipient copies.

sections.title: CONNECT
sections.audit: CONNECT tunnels are not answer endpoints; arbitrary ports can expose SMTP and internal services.

sections.title: OPTIONS
sections.audit: OPTIONS can describe resource capabilities but supplies no standard Email Next capability schema.

sections.title: TRACE
sections.audit: TRACE must not carry secrets and is not an adoption or security probe requirement.

sections.title: Message Context
sections.audit: Context fields do not establish application-level author identity.

sections.title: Request Context Fields
sections.audit: Minimize request context disclosed by message-triggered service access.

sections.title: Expect
sections.audit: 100 Continue is interim permission to send content, not acceptance of the answer.

sections.title: From
sections.audit: HTTP From is contact metadata, explicitly unsuitable for authentication/access control.

sections.title: Referer
sections.audit: Referer can expose context; fragments are excluded but path/query secrets still need protection.

sections.title: TE
sections.audit: TE concerns transfer/trailer handling, not support for application controls.

sections.title: User-Agent
sections.audit: Avoid detailed client fingerprinting; product identity is not capability proof.

sections.title: Response Context Fields
sections.audit: Response context needs method/status-aware interpretation.

sections.title: Allow
sections.audit: Allow advertises currently supported methods, not user authorization to invoke them.

sections.title: Location
sections.audit: Redirects inherit absent fragments; prevent hosted credentials reaching another origin.

sections.title: Retry-After
sections.audit: Retry-After controls timing, not whether repeating the operation is safe.

sections.title: Server
sections.audit: Server strings describe software and can leak detail; do not use them as trust proof.

sections.title: HTTP Authentication
sections.audit: An endpoint profile must select an authentication mechanism; this framework alone selects none.

sections.title: Authentication Scheme
sections.audit: Authentication scheme registration does not establish Email Next principal binding.

sections.title: Authentication Parameters
sections.audit: Parse unique authentication parameters and token68 according to their grammar.

sections.title: Challenge and Response
sections.audit: 401 and 407 challenge different actors; never answer arbitrary challenges with mailbox credentials.

sections.title: Credentials
sections.audit: Valid credentials with insufficient access differ from missing/invalid credentials.

sections.title: Establishing a Protection Space (Realm)
sections.audit: Realm plus origin scopes credentials; shared realms can be broader than one action.

sections.title: Authenticating Users to Origin Servers
sections.audit: Origin authentication is separate from proxy authentication.

sections.title: WWW-Authenticate
sections.audit: 401 includes applicable challenge; multiple schemes require robust parsing.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.audit: Authorization is scoped credentials, not implicit proof of conversation authorship.

sections.title: Authentication-Info
sections.audit: Authentication-Info semantics belong to the chosen scheme; trailers need explicit permission.

sections.title: Authenticating Clients to Proxies
sections.audit: Proxy credentials must remain in their intended proxy scope.

sections.title: Proxy-Authenticate
sections.audit: Proxy-Authenticate concerns the next outbound client, not the email sender.

sections.title: Proxy-Authorization
sections.audit: Proxy-Authorization is consumed by the intended proxy, not forwarded as endpoint credentials.

sections.title: Proxy-Authentication-Info
sections.audit: Proxy authentication completion is not application action completion.

sections.title: Content Negotiation
sections.audit: Negotiated format preference is distinct from negotiated application capability.

sections.title: Proactive Negotiation
sections.audit: Servers may disregard preferences; validate the actual received format.

sections.title: Reactive Negotiation
sections.audit: Alternative links require target and credential checks before following.

sections.title: Request Content Negotiation
sections.audit: Response Accept/Accept-Encoding can describe future request formats without authorizing actions.

sections.title: Content Negotiation Field Features
sections.audit: Preference syntax has absence, weight and wildcard rules.

sections.title: Absence
sections.audit: Absent preferences do not prove support for every actionable format.

sections.title: Quality Values
sections.audit: Quality values range from zero to one with at most three fractional digits.

sections.title: Wildcard Values
sections.audit: Wildcards do not guarantee the server will honor preferences.

sections.title: Content Negotiation Fields
sections.audit: Evaluate actual response metadata rather than inferring it from requested preferences.

sections.title: Accept
sections.audit: Specific media ranges override broader ranges; apply verified example correction 7138.

sections.title: Accept-Charset
sections.audit: Accept-Charset is deprecated; do not build a new fingerprinting capability exchange around it.

sections.title: Accept-Encoding
sections.audit: Missing and empty Accept-Encoding differ; request support is resource/method-specific.

sections.title: Accept-Language
sections.audit: Language preference must remain under user control and can reveal sensitive information.

sections.title: Vary
sections.audit: Vary expands cache selection; it is not a substitute for authorization/privacy cache rules.

sections.title: Conditional Requests
sections.audit: Conditional requests avoid lost updates but do not supply durable action deduplication.

sections.title: Preconditions
sections.audit: Preconditions compare selected resource state, not global conversation history.

sections.title: If-Match
sections.audit: If-Match uses strong comparison; apparent prior application may yield 2xx, so require exact receipt identity.

sections.title: If-None-Match
sections.audit: If-None-Match uses weak comparison; star can guard initial creation, not prove previous content equivalence.

sections.title: If-Modified-Since
sections.audit: If-Modified-Since is ignored when If-None-Match is present and only applies to GET/HEAD.

sections.title: If-Unmodified-Since
sections.audit: Date preconditions have lower precision and can permit apparent-already-applied success.

sections.title: If-Range
sections.audit: If-Range needs a strong validator; a mismatch yields a complete response, not appendable partial bytes.

sections.title: Evaluation of Preconditions
sections.audit: Apply preconditions at the correct processing stage and precedence.

sections.title: When to Evaluate
sections.audit: Authentication/routing errors precede conditions; conditionals do not bypass authorization.

sections.title: Precedence of Preconditions
sections.audit: Follow specified precedence rather than treating all conditions as independent Boolean tests.

sections.title: Range Requests
sections.audit: Range support is optional and can fall back to a complete representation.

sections.title: Range Units
sections.audit: Range unit names are case-insensitive and independently registered.

sections.title: Range Specifiers
sections.audit: Validate ranges and apply verified OWS correction 7306.

sections.title: Byte Ranges
sections.audit: Byte offsets are inclusive over encoded representation bytes; guard numeric overflow.

sections.title: Range
sections.audit: Range can be ignored, rejected or partly satisfied; inspect actual results.

sections.title: Accept-Ranges
sections.audit: Accept-Ranges is advice, not a promise for the next request.

sections.title: Content-Range
sections.audit: Validate bounds and unit before recombining; unknown complete length does not prove completeness.

sections.title: Partial PUT
sections.audit: Partial PUT is not generally interoperable and can overwrite a whole resource on old implementations.

sections.title: Media Type multipart/byteranges
sections.audit: Parse each multipart range independently; illustrative example has an invalid Last-Modified date.

sections.title: Status Codes
sections.audit: Status codes describe HTTP outcomes; application receipts still bind exact submission identity.

sections.title: Overview of Status Codes
sections.audit: Unknown codes retain class semantics; heuristic caching varies by code and method.

sections.title: Informational 1xx
sections.audit: Interim responses are not final action outcomes.

sections.title: 100 Continue
sections.audit: 100 permits continued transfer without proving application success.

sections.title: 101 Switching Protocols
sections.audit: 101 switches only an agreed protocol on the existing connection.

sections.title: Successful 2xx
sections.audit: Success class alone does not distinguish pending work from completed work.

sections.title: 200 OK
sections.audit: 200 content meaning depends on request method; validate the application result.

sections.title: 201 Created
sections.audit: 201 identifies created resource(s), not necessarily completion of downstream business work.

sections.title: 202 Accepted
sections.audit: 202 is explicitly noncommittal; retain pending state and a defined status-query mechanism.

sections.title: 203 Non-Authoritative Information
sections.audit: 203 can describe transformed content; do not silently trust it as original signed bytes.

sections.title: 204 No Content
sections.audit: 204 cannot carry content or trailers; a receipt-body profile cannot accept it as an equivalent receipt.

sections.title: 205 Reset Content
sections.audit: 205 requests view reset; it does not authorize erasing conversation evidence.

sections.title: 206 Partial Content
sections.audit: 206 is partial retrieval; inspect ranges and total completeness.

sections.title: Single Part
sections.audit: Single-range responses require Content-Range; example byte count is consistent.

sections.title: Multiple Parts
sections.audit: Multipart range order/coalescing may differ from the request; inspect each part.

sections.title: Combining Parts
sections.audit: Combine partial responses only with the same strong validator and complete coverage rules.

sections.title: Redirection 3xx
sections.audit: Redirects can change method/target/credential scope; do not follow blindly for submissions.

sections.title: 300 Multiple Choices
sections.audit: 300 alternatives are not a standard machine-readable action negotiation format.

sections.title: 301 Moved Permanently
sections.audit: 301 may turn POST into GET; no implicit resubmission or migration of credentials.

sections.title: 302 Found
sections.audit: 302 may turn POST into GET and is temporary.

sections.title: 303 See Other
sections.audit: 303 retrieves an indirect result; the destination is not equivalent to the original target.

sections.title: 304 Not Modified
sections.audit: 304 reuses a previously stored representation and carries no new content or trailers.

sections.title: 305 Use Proxy
sections.audit: 305 is deprecated; do not configure a proxy from it.

sections.title: 306 (Unused)
sections.audit: 306 is reserved and unused.

sections.title: 307 Temporary Redirect
sections.audit: 307 preserves method when followed; preservation does not authorize a new recipient.

sections.title: 308 Permanent Redirect
sections.audit: 308 preserves method per verified erratum 7109; permanent redirect is not principal migration.

sections.title: Client Error 4xx
sections.audit: Client error class requires code-specific interpretation, not a universal rollback assumption.

sections.title: 400 Bad Request
sections.audit: 400 can reflect malformed framing or deceptive routing; retain diagnostics without treating them as instructions.

sections.title: 401 Unauthorized
sections.audit: 401 explicitly means this request was not applied; previous attempts may still need reconciliation.

sections.title: 402 Payment Required
sections.audit: 402 is reserved, not a specified payment workflow.

sections.title: 403 Forbidden
sections.audit: 403 refuses access; do not automatically retry with identical credentials.

sections.title: 404 Not Found
sections.audit: 404 may conceal existence; it does not prove no prior submission or permanent absence.

sections.title: 405 Method Not Allowed
sections.audit: 405 requires Allow and can be cached; support is resource-specific.

sections.title: 406 Not Acceptable
sections.audit: 406 supplies negotiation failure, not permission to reinterpret arbitrary HTML as a receipt.

sections.title: 407 Proxy Authentication Required
sections.audit: 407 requests proxy authentication, never endpoint or mailbox credentials interchangeably.

sections.title: 408 Request Timeout
sections.audit: 408 reports incomplete request and permits retry; distinguish it from a local observation timeout.

sections.title: 409 Conflict
sections.audit: 409 reports state conflict; a reused submission ID with different content needs explicit conflict semantics.

sections.title: 410 Gone
sections.audit: 410 means likely permanent unavailability, not verified deletion of all stored copies.

sections.title: 411 Length Required
sections.audit: 411 permits adding valid Content-Length; preserve the application identity and payload.

sections.title: 412 Precondition Failed
sections.audit: 412 signals false precondition; it does not identify a prior successful attempt.

sections.title: 413 Content Too Large
sections.audit: 413 refuses oversized content; temporary retry advice does not waive deduplication rules.

sections.title: 414 URI Too Long
sections.audit: 414 must not trigger moving sensitive fields into a different unapproved destination.

sections.title: 415 Unsupported Media Type
sections.audit: 415 distinguishes unsupported media type/content coding; do not blindly change signed bytes.

sections.title: 416 Range Not Satisfiable
sections.audit: 416 can report unsatisfiable or excessive ranges; full response remains possible when Range is ignored.

sections.title: 417 Expectation Failed
sections.audit: 417 concerns expectations and is distinct from answer rejection.

sections.title: 418 (Unused)
sections.audit: 418 is reserved; no Email Next use is proposed.

sections.title: 421 Misdirected Request
sections.audit: 421 permits retry over another connection even for non-idempotent methods; preserve target authorization.

sections.title: 422 Unprocessable Content
sections.audit: 422 distinguishes valid syntax from unusable instructions.

sections.title: 426 Upgrade Required
sections.audit: 426 requires Upgrade; the illustrative HTTP/3.0 token is not a deployment recipe for transport migration.

sections.title: Server Error 5xx
sections.audit: Server/gateway failures can leave upstream application outcome unknown.

sections.title: 500 Internal Server Error
sections.audit: 500 does not establish that all application effects rolled back.

sections.title: 501 Not Implemented
sections.audit: 501 reports unsupported server functionality and can be heuristically cached.

sections.title: 502 Bad Gateway
sections.audit: 502 reports an invalid upstream response, not necessarily nonexecution upstream.

sections.title: 503 Service Unavailable
sections.audit: 503 may provide retry timing; an unavailable server need not return it.

sections.title: 504 Gateway Timeout
sections.audit: 504 reports missing timely upstream response; preserve unknown outcome until reconciled.

sections.title: 505 HTTP Version Not Supported
sections.audit: 505 concerns HTTP major version, not Email Next feature enrollment.

sections.title: Extending HTTP
sections.audit: Prefer existing version-independent extension points; application features do not need a new HTTP version.

sections.title: Method Extensibility
sections.audit: New methods require generic semantics rather than application-specific verbs.

sections.title: Method Registry
sections.audit: Method registration requires IETF Review; no new method is allocated here.

sections.title: Considerations for New Methods
sections.audit: New methods must define safety, idempotency, caching, content and conditional behavior.

sections.title: Status Code Extensibility
sections.audit: Existing status meanings cannot be overridden by an application profile.

sections.title: Status Code Registry
sections.audit: New status registrations require IETF Review; no code is allocated here.

sections.title: Considerations for New Status Codes
sections.audit: Application result details belong in an explicit format unless generic new status semantics are justified.

sections.title: Field Extensibility
sections.audit: Unknown fields may be ignored; required behavior needs explicit supported-profile evidence.

sections.title: Field Name Registry
sections.audit: HTTP fields have a separate registry from email fields; permanent registration is Specification Required.

sections.title: Considerations for New Fields
sections.audit: New fields need scope, trailer, intermediary, redirect and privacy rules.

sections.title: Considerations for New Field Names
sections.audit: Use descriptive scoped names and avoid X- and ambiguous underscore mappings.

sections.title: Considerations for New Field Values
sections.audit: Define duplicate/singleton behavior and comma encoding explicitly.

sections.title: Authentication Scheme Extensibility
sections.audit: Authentication extensions must preserve framework semantics.

sections.title: Authentication Scheme Registry
sections.audit: Authentication scheme registration requires IETF Review.

sections.title: Considerations for New Authentication Schemes
sections.audit: Requests carry authentication context; custom credential fields need explicit cache controls.

sections.title: Range Unit Extensibility
sections.audit: No new range unit is needed merely for button submissions.

sections.title: Range Unit Registry
sections.audit: Range-unit registration requires IETF Review.

sections.title: Considerations for New Range Units
sections.audit: Any future unit must define content-coding/intermediary interactions.

sections.title: Content Coding Extensibility
sections.audit: Content-coding extension is independent of conversation operation encoding.

sections.title: Content Coding Registry
sections.audit: Registration prevents incompatible reuse of transfer/content coding names.

sections.title: Considerations for New Content Codings
sections.audit: Coding parameters should be self-describing rather than depend on lost metadata.

sections.title: Upgrade Token Registry
sections.audit: Upgrade tokens are registered independently; registration does not provide deployment evidence.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: HTTP security requirements complement, not replace, application authorization and encrypted-mail boundaries.

sections.title: Establishing Authority
sections.audit: Verify authority and show destination; origin branding and stored credentials can enable phishing.

sections.title: Risks of Intermediaries
sections.audit: Intermediaries and caches remain trust boundaries; HTTP does not make their operators trustworthy.

sections.title: Attacks Based on File and Path Names
sections.audit: Do not map untrusted URI/file names directly to local storage paths.

sections.title: Attacks Based on Command, Code, or Query Injection
sections.audit: Treat request fields/content and stored diagnostics as data, never executable instructions.

sections.title: Attacks via Protocol Element Length
sections.audit: Bound parsing, slow input and numeric conversions without inventing protocol-wide quotas.

sections.title: Attacks Using Shared-Dictionary Compression
sections.audit: Separate secret and attacker-controlled compression contexts or disable sensitive compression.

sections.title: Disclosure of Personal Information
sections.audit: Avoid disclosing mailbox identity, credentials and browsing state during endpoint access.

sections.title: Privacy of Server Log Information
sections.audit: Logs can identify reading patterns even with pseudonyms; minimize and protect retained traces.

sections.title: Disclosure of Sensitive Information in URIs
sections.audit: URLs leak through history/logs/sharing; bearer-link exposure is a deliberate weaker access model.

sections.title: Application Handling of Field Names
sections.audit: Field-name normalization must not alias hyphens/underscores into conflicting security values.

sections.title: Disclosure of Fragment after Redirects
sections.audit: Redirected fragments can be read by destination scripts; hosted-entry redirect restrictions address this risk.

sections.title: Disclosure of Product Information
sections.audit: Limit product/internal-host information; version strings do not establish security assurance.

sections.title: Browser Fingerprinting
sections.audit: Detailed negotiation fingerprints users; minimize advertised preferences.

sections.title: Validator Retention
sections.audit: ETags are not malicious-change protection and can track users across requests.

sections.title: Denial-of-Service Attacks Using Range
sections.audit: Many overlapping ranges amplify resource use; reject/coalesce as appropriate.

sections.title: Authentication Considerations
sections.audit: Scheme-specific security review remains required.

sections.title: Confidentiality of Credentials
sections.audit: Secure credentials before transmission; authentication alone does not prevent replay.

sections.title: Credentials and Idle Clients
sections.audit: HTTP has no universal logout/credential-discard command; define expiry/revocation separately.

sections.title: Protection Spaces
sections.audit: Shared-origin realms can expose credentials across tenants; isolate or narrowly scope access.

sections.title: Additional Response Fields
sections.audit: Authentication response metadata can itself expose identity/protocol use.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.audit: Existing registrations are recorded; this draft makes no new allocation claim.

sections.title: URI Scheme Registration
sections.audit: http/https schemes retain their registered meaning.

sections.title: Method Registration
sections.audit: Method safety/idempotency table is preserved; wildcard method remains reserved.

sections.title: Status Code Registration
sections.audit: Status registry entries do not define application receipt schemas.

sections.title: Field Name Registration
sections.audit: HTTP fields moved out of email registries; Content-MD5 is obsoleted in HTTP.

sections.title: Authentication Scheme Registration
sections.audit: No authentication scheme is defined by RFC 9110 itself.

sections.title: Content Coding Registration
sections.audit: Coding registration includes deprecated aliases and reserved identity.

sections.title: Range Unit Registration
sections.audit: bytes and reserved none are distinguished.

sections.title: Media Type Registration
sections.audit: multipart/byteranges registration and q-parameter reservation apply.

sections.title: Port Registration
sections.audit: Port registrations do not grant endpoint authorization.

sections.title: Upgrade Token Registration
sections.audit: HTTP Upgrade token registration does not negotiate transport by itself.

sections.title: References
sections.audit: Reference entries were read; dependency reading is a separate obligation.

sections.title: Normative References
sections.audit: Caching, URI, TLS, certificate identity, MIME, grammar and encoding dependencies require their own dispositions.

sections.title: Informative References
sections.audit: Protocol versions, cookies, authority delegation and web security dependencies remain distinct follow-ups.

sections.title: Collected ABNF
sections.audit: Complete grammar reviewed; sender list expansion differs from tolerant receipt, and reported erratum 9164 describes equivalent normalization.

sections.title: Changes from Previous RFCs
sections.audit: Every predecessor change subsection reviewed with verified corrections below.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: Inline blob methods reduce round trips and add reverse lookup; they do not authenticate message resources.

sections.title: Conventions Used in This Document
sections.audit: Core JMAP types and requirement conventions reviewed.

sections.title: Addition to the Capabilities Object
sections.audit: Blob capability has session and per-account placement.

sections.title: urn:ietf:params:jmap:blob
sections.audit: Creation-size/source-count limits and supported types/digests are account capabilities; at least64 sources supported. Null size limit does not guarantee resource availability or remove client bounds.

sections.title: Capability Example
sections.audit: Capability example reviewed; server digest preference is not Email Next cryptographic algorithm policy.

sections.title: Blob Methods
sections.audit: Blob/copy remains core; blobs are arbitrary octet sequences.

sections.title: Blob/upload
sections.audit: Upload concatenates ordered sources; invalid ranges/data fail the creation without guessing. Created IDs support later methods; expiry semantics remain core JMAP. Media type is a hint.

sections.title: Blob/upload Simple Example
sections.audit: Wrapped base64 is a publication convenience, not wire whitespace permission.

sections.title: Blob/upload Complex Example
sections.audit: Concatenation/backreferences reviewed; example omits required accountId inputs and includes oldState despite stateless prose. Do not use as a complete request fixture unchanged.

sections.title: Blob/get
sections.audit: Get permits short ranges with isTruncated; size is whole-blob size, while digest is selected returned octets. Invalid UTF-8 yields encoding diagnostics and base64 where requested.

sections.title: Blob/get Simple Example
sections.audit: Full and ranged published SHA1 digests plus ranged SHA256 digest independently reproduced from literal example bytes; this is not an authentication check.

sections.title: Blob/get Example with Range and Encoding Errors
sections.audit: Range/encoding examples reviewed; explicit text-error response omits required null text field and upload type results appear inconsistent with supplied hints. Normative rules govern fixtures.

sections.title: Blob/lookup
sections.audit: Reverse lookup respects account/type capabilities; inaccessible or nonexistent blobs yield indistinguishable empty matches. Containment is directional, not arbitrary graph reachability.

sections.title: Blob/lookup Example
sections.audit: Example uses notFound despite earlier indistinguishable empty-array rule; record conflict and do not adopt an existence-leaking response distinction.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: Apply access control to lookup, distrust supplied media types, scan composed results where applicable and bound digest costs; these are provider controls, not endpoint authentication.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.audit: Capability, error and data-type registrations reviewed separately from current registry state.

sections.title: JMAP Capability Registration for "blob"
sections.audit: Registers blob capability.

sections.title: JMAP Error Codes Registration for "unknownDataType"
sections.audit: UnknownDataType covers unknown names or missing required capability.

sections.title: Creation of "JMAP Data Types" Registry
sections.audit: Creates specification-required data-type registry with blob/state-change flags; initial table is not a live registry snapshot.

sections.title: References
sections.audit: Complete reference lists, acknowledgments and author end matter reviewed.

sections.title: Normative References
sections.audit: Core JMAP, base64, digest and requirement references remain separately scoped; digest-registry successor applicability requires review.

sections.title: Informative References
sections.audit: IMAP literal, registration, JMAP Mail and MDN references do not define Email Next resource manifests.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: Asynchronous group key establishment supports offline recipients; does not supply application identity or delivery semantics.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.audit: All terms reviewed; client is a cryptographic endpoint, not necessarily one person.

sections.title: Presentation Language
sections.audit: TLS presentation language plus MLS-specific encodings reviewed.

sections.title: Optional Value
sections.audit: Presence byte accepts only zero or one.

sections.title: Variable-Size Vector Length Headers
sections.audit: Minimal 1/2/4-byte lengths required; prefix 11 invalid; wire maximum does not authorize unbounded allocation.

sections.title: Protocol Overview
sections.audit: Trusted authentication service distinguished from largely untrusted delivery service.

sections.title: Cryptographic State and Evolution
sections.audit: Ratchet tree, key schedule and secret tree have separate responsibilities.

sections.title: Example Protocol Execution
sections.audit: All flows reviewed; proposals do not apply changes until committed; regular updates and access control are application responsibilities.

sections.title: External Joins
sections.audit: External joining needs current GroupInfo and application authorization.

sections.title: Relationships between Epochs
sections.audit: Reinitialization, branching and resumption links reviewed; they do not imply history disclosure.

sections.title: Ratchet Tree Concepts
sections.audit: Tree structure supports efficient exclusion and updates.

sections.title: Ratchet Tree Terminology
sections.audit: Complete binary tree terminology; internal representation unconstrained.

sections.title: Ratchet Tree Nodes
sections.audit: Resolution ordering, blanks and unmerged leaves reviewed with examples.

sections.title: Paths through a Ratchet Tree
sections.audit: Direct, copath and filtered paths reviewed with full table.

sections.title: Views of a Ratchet Tree
sections.audit: Tree invariant restricts private-key knowledge; descendants need not know every ancestor key.

sections.title: Cryptographic Objects
sections.audit: All cryptographic object definitions read.

sections.title: Cipher Suites
sections.audit: Single suite selects HPKE, hash, MAC and signature primitives.

sections.title: Public Keys
sections.audit: Opaque public-key formats depend on selected primitive.

sections.title: Signing
sections.audit: Signature algorithms and labeled signing structures reviewed.

sections.title: Public Key Encryption
sections.audit: HPKE Base mode uses labeled context; ciphertext purposes remain distinct.

sections.title: Hash-Based Identifiers
sections.audit: KeyPackage and proposal references hash distinct labeled encodings; KDF wording requires reconciliation.

sections.title: Credentials
sections.audit: Basic credential is bare identity assertion; application supplies reference identity and validation.

sections.title: Credential Validation
sections.audit: All credential-introduction events require AS validation; replacement additionally requires authorized succession.

sections.title: Credential Expiry and Revocation
sections.audit: Expiry, renewal, historical signatures and revocation need distinct application policies.

sections.title: Uniquely Identifying Clients
sections.audit: Leaf index epoch-scoped; account identity may span devices; application_id is not AS-authenticated.

sections.title: Message Framing
sections.audit: All structures read; application messages require PrivateMessage.

sections.title: Content Authentication
sections.audit: Sender-specific keys, signed context and commit confirmation reviewed; AEAD alone insufficient.

sections.title: Encoding and Decoding a Public Message
sections.audit: Public member messages require membership tag and valid authentication data.

sections.title: Encoding and Decoding a Private Message
sections.audit: Private framing leaves group, epoch, type and authenticated_data visible.

sections.title: Content Encryption
sections.audit: Zero padding, unused generation, persistent state, reuse guard and AEAD bounds reviewed.

sections.title: Sender Data Encryption
sections.audit: Sender data derives protection from ciphertext sample; indicated leaf must be non-blank.

sections.title: Ratchet Tree Operations
sections.audit: All tree operations reviewed.

sections.title: Parent Node Contents
sections.audit: Parent public key/hash and sorted unmerged-leaf indices reviewed.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: RFC5646 and RFC4647 together form BCP47. This review covers tag formation; matching requires the companion standard.

sections.title: The Language Tag
sections.audit: Tags identify human languages, including signed and constructed languages; they do not identify programming languages.

sections.title: Syntax
sections.audit: Use the complete ASCII grammar, including the fixed grandfathered list. No whitespace or underscores; subtags are at most eight characters, but whole tags have no fixed maximum.

sections.title: Formatting of Language Tags
sections.audit: All tags, including private use and extensions, compare case-insensitively. Use locale-neutral ASCII casing; presentation casing carries no meaning.

sections.title: Language Subtag Sources and Interpretation
sections.audit: The IANA registry, not a current ISO code list alone, defines registered subtags. Position determines type; extension and private-use sequences remain at the end.

sections.title: Primary Language Subtag
sections.audit: Preserve primary-language rules, private-use ranges and historical stable assignments; do not substitute every ISO code as a valid language subtag.

sections.title: Extended Language Subtags
sections.audit: Extlangs use their registered prefix; only one is permitted even though ABNF parses up to three. Prefer the corresponding primary-language form when generating tags.

sections.title: Script Subtag
sections.audit: One script subtag occupies the defined position. Suppress-Script is generation guidance, not a declaration that an explicit script makes a tag invalid.

sections.title: Region Subtag
sections.audit: One region subtag occupies the defined position. Only the selected registered ISO/UN values and private-use ranges apply, not every country or numeric area code.

sections.title: Variant Subtags
sections.audit: Repeated variants are forbidden. Variant prefixes and ordering provide usage guidance; do not convert every SHOULD into a validity rejection.

sections.title: Extension Subtags
sections.audit: Extension singletons must be allocated, unique and followed by content. Internal extension validity requires that extension’s specification and data; base validation need not perform it.

sections.title: Private Use Subtags
sections.audit: Private use can occupy the entire tag or its final sequence; meaning requires private agreement and is not inferred from familiar-looking subtags.

sections.title: Grandfathered and Redundant Registrations
sections.audit: Grandfathered tags remain valid, including irregular forms. Redundant registrations and preferred replacements do not make historical tags invalid.

sections.title: Classes of Conformance
sections.audit: Separate ABNF well-formedness, registry-date validity and extension-specific validity. Apply surrounding section rules as well as the short checklist; erratum 5457 flags its extlang omission.

sections.title: Registry Format and Maintenance
sections.audit: Treat registry content as versioned data with its specified record format, not as executable instructions or a flat list of complete tags.

sections.title: Format of the IANA Language Subtag Registry
sections.audit: Treat registry content as versioned data with its specified record format, not as executable instructions or a flat list of complete tags.

sections.title: File Format
sections.audit: Parse UTF-8 record-jar fields, folding and inclusive ranges; preserve NFC and field boundaries. The registry’s Unicode descriptions do not expand the ASCII tag alphabet.

sections.title: Record and Field Definitions
sections.audit: Record File-Date and distinguish Tag from Subtag records. Respect repeated-field allowances; ignore unknown future fields as recommended.

sections.title: Type Field
sections.audit: Keep type-specific namespaces separate when looking up a subtag.

sections.title: Subtag and Tag Fields
sections.audit: Registry casing is standardized presentation; comparisons remain case-insensitive.

sections.title: Description Field
sections.audit: Descriptions identify records but are not localized UI names. Held erratum 8711 concerns Latin-script descriptions, not the tag alphabet.

sections.title: Deprecated Field
sections.audit: Deprecated tags remain valid; generation is discouraged. Deprecation without Preferred-Value supplies no replacement.

sections.title: Preferred-Value Field
sections.audit: Preferred-Value supports canonicalization and can change through registry maintenance. Replacement does not require retagging existing content.

sections.title: Prefix Field
sections.audit: Distinguish extlang prefix requirements from variant-prefix guidance. Prefix relationships can constrain useful ordering without making arbitrary combinations meaningful.

sections.title: Suppress-Script Field
sections.audit: Suppress-Script guides omission of redundant scripts. Its absence does not prove a language has only one script or a known default script.

sections.title: Macrolanguage Field
sections.audit: Macrolanguage relationships are informational; they do not guarantee mutual intelligibility or an appropriate fallback.

sections.title: Scope Field
sections.audit: Scope distinguishes collections, macrolanguages, special and private-use values. Missing Scope means an individual language.

sections.title: Comments Field
sections.audit: Comments are mutable explanatory material, not a stable validation rule.

sections.title: Language Subtag Reviewer
sections.audit: Reviewer authority, maintenance and appeals govern registry changes; a rendering implementation consumes the resulting registry instead of bypassing it.

sections.title: Maintenance of the Registry
sections.audit: Reviewer authority, maintenance and appeals govern registry changes; a rendering implementation consumes the resulting registry instead of bypassing it.

sections.title: Stability of IANA Registry Entries
sections.audit: Stable identifiers and retained deprecated entries protect old content. Preferred mappings and other fields can change, so canonicalization needs identified data.

sections.title: Registration Procedure for Subtags
sections.audit: Use the registration process for new public assignments; this proposal registers none. Historical contact details are not a current integration endpoint.

sections.title: Possibilities for Registration
sections.audit: Use the registration process for new public assignments; this proposal registers none. Historical contact details are not a current integration endpoint.

sections.title: Extensions and the Extensions Registry
sections.audit: Extension assignment, versioning and canonicalization are separate contracts. Identify extension data revisions if extension-specific validation is chosen.

sections.title: Update of the Language Subtag Registry
sections.audit: RFC5645 describes the initial registry update; it does not substitute for an identified subsequent registry snapshot.

sections.title: Applicability of the Subtag Registry
sections.audit: The registry is not a language picker, localized-name database, fallback map or complete model of language relationships.

sections.title: Formation and Processing of Language Tags
sections.audit: Tag content with justified specificity. Any selection rules departing from this guidance need an explicit profile explanation; no such policy is selected by this audit.

sections.title: Choice of Language Tag
sections.audit: Tag content with justified specificity. Any selection rules departing from this guidance need an explicit profile explanation; no such policy is selected by this audit.

sections.title: Tagging Encompassed Languages
sections.audit: Prefer the known encompassed language, but do not infer intelligibility from a shared macrolanguage.

sections.title: Using Extended Language Subtags
sections.audit: Extlang forms support compatibility. A macrolanguage tag remains valid; region alone does not uniquely identify an encompassed language.

sections.title: Meaning of the Language Tag
sections.audit: A valid tag need not describe a plausible language/script/region combination. HTML span language differs from document audience metadata; tags do not guarantee character repertoire.

sections.title: Lists of Languages
sections.audit: Language lists have application-specific scope. Do not treat a list of tags as one HTML lang value.

sections.title: Length Considerations
sections.audit: There is no universal maximum whole-tag length; any profile limit is an additional documented choice.

sections.title: Working with Limited Buffer Sizes
sections.audit: A fixed buffer limit must accommodate at least 35 characters; 35 is a minimum capacity, not a maximum valid length. Document overflow behavior.

sections.title: Truncation of Language Tags
sections.audit: Truncation changes meaning. If permitted, remove complete rightmost subtags and stranded singletons rather than slicing characters.

sections.title: Canonicalization of Language Tags
sections.audit: Canonicalization orders extension sequences and applies preferred mappings, including removing extlang form. Case normalization and variant reordering are separate optional steps; deprecated values without replacements can remain canonical.

sections.title: Considerations for Private Use Subtags
sections.audit: Private-use ranges retain structural information but no public agreed meaning. Do not derive identity, geography or authorization from private values.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.audit: File-Date identifies registry publication; keep data available locally rather than requiring a network lookup for each message.

sections.title: Language Subtag Registry
sections.audit: File-Date identifies registry publication; keep data available locally rather than requiring a network lookup for each message.

sections.title: Extensions Registry
sections.audit: The extension registry identifies maintaining authorities and specifications; it does not contain each extension’s full value vocabulary.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.audit: Language metadata can disclose sensitive inferences. Guard resource use; tags do not prevent homographs. Rendering must not require registry availability or fetch arbitrary extension URLs.

sections.title: Character Set Considerations
sections.audit: Language tags are ASCII metadata; font selection and rendering behavior are outside this RFC and need the HTML/rendering contract.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 4646
sections.audit: Use operative grammar and rules rather than change-summary wording. The summary says grandfathered production was removed although the published grammar retains it.

sections.title: References
sections.audit: References identify dependencies; their listing is not a full review of RFC4647, ISO standards, Unicode or extension specifications.

sections.audit: Registration-form examples illustrate procedure, not current language-tag validation or authority to submit a registration.

sections.title: HPKE, including all 5.1–5.3 subsections
sections.audit: Base mode does not authenticate the sender. Preserve setup binding, validation, sequence/nonce state, errors and exporter separation. Other modes are not automatically selected.
sections.review_provenance: Captured source text reviewed; test vectors not executed.

sections.title: Single-Shot APIs, including 6.1–6.2
sections.audit: Stateless templates do not supply application replay protection. Verified6941 corrects the mode reference.
sections.review_provenance: Captured source text reviewed; test vectors not executed.

sections.title: Algorithm Identifiers, including all 7.1–7.3 subsections
sections.audit: Selected suite controls KEM/KDF/AEAD; retain serialization, key derivation, input validation and length constraints. Errata7121,7934,7937 and held7251 qualify fixtures and parameters.
sections.review_provenance: Captured source text reviewed; test vectors not executed.

sections.title: API Considerations, including 8.1–8.2
sections.audit: Authenticated application binding and exact error behavior remain required at the library boundary; errors never authorize plaintext fallback.
sections.review_provenance: Captured source text reviewed; test vectors not executed.

sections.title: Security Considerations, including all 9.1–9.9 subsections
sections.audit: HPKE alone supplies neither replay/downgrade handling nor unordered delivery or forward secrecy against recipient-key compromise. Preserve randomness and metadata boundaries. Verified7790 excludes Insider-Auth; selected suite is not post-quantum.
sections.review_provenance: Captured source text reviewed; test vectors not executed.

sections.title: Message Encoding

sections.review_provenance: Captured source text reviewed; test vectors not executed.

sections.title: Title, status, abstract and contents
sections.audit: Frontmatter and contents read; standards-track source.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: Associated data is authenticated but not encrypted.

sections.title: Background
sections.audit: AEAD integrates confidentiality and integrity; not mailbox ownership.

sections.title: Scope
sections.audit: Interface excludes anti-replay and access-control policy.

sections.title: Benefits
sections.audit: Use established AEAD interface rather than invent cipher/MAC composition.

sections.title: Conventions Used in This Document
sections.audit: RFC2119 requirement vocabulary.

sections.title: AEAD Interface
sections.audit: Inputs/outputs are octet strings; extensions must preserve interoperability.

sections.title: Authenticated Encryption
sections.audit: Distinct nonces per key; selected GCM cannot use zero-length alternative. Length failures return only errors, never partial data; secret key not explicitly copied to other inputs.

sections.title: Authenticated Decryption
sections.audit: Plaintext or FAIL only; verified4008 corrects ciphertext C in descriptive input list.

sections.title: Data Formatting
sections.audit: Encoding belongs to enclosing protocol; preceding nonce/data recommended for processing.

sections.title: Guidance on the Use of AEAD Algorithms
sections.audit: Nonce uniqueness is mandatory; zero-length nonce requires compatible algorithm, not GCM.

sections.title: Requirements on Nonce Generation
sections.audit: Coordinate shared-key devices; persist future nonce before use; verified4268 clarifies next reserved range.

sections.title: Recommended Nonce Formation
sections.audit: Fixed/counter recommendation is not replacement for selected MLS/HPKE nonce construction; reported6415 not adopted.

sections.title: Partially Implicit Nonces
sections.audit: All figure and ESP rationale read; reported4338 is unverified, ESP not selected.

sections.title: Construction of AEAD Inputs
sections.audit: AAD and structured plaintext must be unambiguously parseable without unauthenticated parsing dependencies.

sections.title: Example Usage

sections.title: Introduction
sections.audit: Delegated service access replaces sharing the account password with the mail client; it does not itself identify an Email Next principal.

sections.title: Roles

sections.title: Protocol Flow
sections.audit: Apply the authorization→grant→token→resource sequence; explicit device linking is an additional independently checked step.

sections.title: Authorization Grant
sections.audit: Select authorization code only; the other grant families are not automatic compatibility fallbacks.

sections.title: Authorization Code
sections.audit: Use short-lived single-use codes bound to client and exact redirect, supplemented by S256 PKCE.

sections.title: Implicit
sections.audit: Do not select browser-delivered implicit access tokens; apply RFC9700's current security guidance.

sections.title: Resource Owner Password Credentials
sections.audit: Do not collect the resource-owner password in the mail client; RFC9700 prohibits this grant.

sections.title: Client Credentials
sections.audit: Do not substitute client-credentials authority for a human account's consent or principal link.

sections.title: Access Token
sections.audit: Use opaque scoped, expiring access tokens; possession remains bearer authority, not device proof.

sections.title: Refresh Token
sections.audit: Keep refresh credentials at the token endpoint and rotate their family; never send them to service actions.

sections.title: TLS Version
sections.audit: Historical TLS advice is superseded by RFC8996/9700 and the selected TLS profile.

sections.title: HTTP Redirections
sections.audit: Authorization browser redirects are separate from service submission's no-redirect rule; do not forward credential POSTs with 307.

sections.title: Interoperability
sections.audit: Fill the framework's discovery/registration choices with trusted registration, not endpoints inferred from mail.

sections.title: Notational Conventions
sections.audit: BCP14, ABNF and URI terminology apply; their appearance here does not complete transitive source review.

sections.title: Client Registration

sections.title: Client Types
sections.audit: Treat the native client as public; a shipped shared secret cannot make it confidential.

sections.title: Client Identifier
sections.audit: Send the registered client_id as an identifier, never as proof of client or account identity.

sections.title: Client Authentication
sections.audit: Do not claim public-client authentication from client_id. Stronger client authentication requires a separately selected method.

sections.title: Client Password

sections.title: Other Authentication Methods

sections.audit: Bind endpoints in trusted registration. Authorization, token and resource destinations have distinct credential rules.

sections.title: Authorization Endpoint

sections.title: Response Type

sections.title: Redirection Endpoint
sections.audit: Bind the exact chosen loopback callback to the pending attempt under RFC8252's native exception.

sections.title: Endpoint Request Confidentiality
sections.audit: Use local loopback HTTP only for the selected native callback; all remote authorization/token traffic requires TLS.

sections.title: Registration Requirements
sections.audit: Register the callback host/path independently, allowing only the selected ephemeral-port exception.

sections.title: Dynamic Configuration
sections.audit: Do not adopt broad partial-URI matching; apply current exact matching and the explicit native port exception.

sections.title: Invalid Endpoint
sections.audit: Reject invalid client/redirect requests locally at the service; never redirect an error to an unvalidated URI.

sections.title: Endpoint Content
sections.audit: Return minimal callback content without third-party resources; keep code/state out of exposed page content and logs.

sections.title: Token Endpoint
sections.audit: Send form-encoded token requests only to the registered TLS token endpoint; reject unsupported grants.

sections.title: Client Authentication
sections.audit: Public clients provide client_id; code/client/redirect/PKCE binding supplies the selected redemption checks, not a static secret.

sections.title: Access Token Scope

sections.title: Obtaining Authorization
sections.audit: Only the code path below is a selected means of obtaining user authorization.

sections.title: Authorization Code Grant
sections.audit: Use code plus S256, issuer and transaction binding; code possession alone does not authorize an Email Next principal.

sections.title: Authorization Request
sections.audit: Bind client_id, exact chosen redirect, scope, state and PKCE challenge to one pending attempt before opening consent.

sections.title: Authorization Response
sections.audit: Validate state, required issuer response and original callback URI before redeeming a short-lived one-use code.

sections.title: Error Response

sections.title: Access Token Request

sections.title: Access Token Response

sections.title: APPEND Command
sections.audit: APPEND stores one message, can re-encode eight-bit input and rolls back failed appends. It cannot submit SMTP recipients. Treat draft exceptions carefully, not as permission to send invalid protected messages.

sections.title: SEARCH Command
sections.audit: Search combines criteria and may omit non-text/non-message MIME terminals. Decode comparisons under erratum 261. String search is case-insensitive substring matching, date searches ignore time/zone, flags remain mutable, and empty HEADER search tests presence. None proves exact identity or complete history.

sections.title: STORE Command

sections.title: COPY Command

sections.title: UID Command
sections.audit: Missing UIDs yield successful no-ops. FETCH prefixes remain sequence numbers and UID-command FETCH responses include UID. Ranges are order-independent, including `n:*`; inspect returned UIDs.
